entries.title: Three-Point Lighting
entries.text:
Three-Point Lighting

Three-point lighting, the basic three point lighting setup, places a key, a fill, and a backlight so a face is modeled from one dominant side, opened in the shadows, and separated from the background. The key is brightest and sets direction; fill and back exist only as ratios against it.

Create this Three-Point Lighting

Narrative function

In a scene it is the default portrait grammar: the audience can read both eyes, the cheekbones have a light side and a shadow side, and the hair does not melt into the wall. Classical coverage uses it so reverse shots match, and so a close-up still feels like the same room as the master.

It is the wrong tool when the room already has a single honest source, or when the story wants a face half-erased. Teaching the setup is useful.

Leaving it on every night interior as three hidden movie lights is how a crime scene starts to look like a cosmetics ad.

How it works

Place the key about 45 degrees off camera axis and 30 to 45 degrees above the eyes, large enough to be slightly soft unless the scene is harsh. 5 to 3 stops down so the shadow cheek still has pores.

Put backlight high and behind, often slightly opposite the key, warm or white, flagged so it rims hair and shoulders without flaring the lens. Prompt: Classic three-point lighting on [Subject]: key at 45 degrees, soft fill opening shadows, warm backlight rim, modeled volume.

When to use it

Use it for a teachable talking-head or a studio close-up that must stay readable across a whole scene. Do not use it as the only language of a night interior that is supposed to be one lamp.

Compared with similar shots

Key light is the dominant source inside this setup, not the setup itself. Fill light only opens the key's shadows; it has no third direction.

Backlight is the rear unit that separates the figure. Rembrandt lighting and loop lighting are facial patterns you can make with the key while the other two points still exist.

Key LightDecide where the world is lit from. Everything else follows.

Fill LightControl how much of the dark you can still read.

BacklightSeparate a dark figure from a dark world.

In film

Casablanca and Rebecca show the classical Hollywood version: key, fill, and a hair or back edge kept in ratio so stars stay modeled in every size. Use that grammar, not a poster to copy.

Later films keep the three jobs even when the units are hidden in practicals.

Prompt it

Name all three jobs, not the word portrait. " Add key side (left or right), fill ratio, and backlight color.

Do not write a mood word in place of the three positions.

Use in Image Generator

Classic three-point lighting on [Subject]: key at 45 degrees, soft fill opening shadows, warm backlight rim, sculpted dimensionality.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a single frontal soft light labeled as three-point. The tell is even cheeks, no hair edge, and a shadowless nose.

Fix it by offsetting the key, dropping fill, and adding a flagged rear rim.

Questions

What is three-point lighting in film?

A conventional arrangement of key, fill, and backlight. The key sets direction and exposure, fill opens the shadow side, and backlight separates the subject from the background.

Three-point lighting vs key light

Key light is one source. Three-point lighting is a three-job system in which that key is joined by a dimmer fill and a rear separation light.

When should I use three-point lighting?

Use it when a face must stay fully readable and consistent across coverage. Skip it when a single motivated source should own the room.

How do I prompt three-point lighting for AI image or video?

State key at about 45 degrees, soft fill on the opposite cheek, and a warm or white backlight rim. Name which side is keyed so the model does not flatten the face.

entries.title: Key Light
entries.text:
Key Light

A key light in key light cinematography is the principal source that sets the subject's dominant direction, shape, and exposure. Shadows fall away from it; every other light is measured against it.

Create this Key Light

Narrative function

Deciding the key is deciding where the world is lit from. A window, a bare bulb, the sun, or a hidden unit standing in for those things will tell the audience what time it is and who is exposed.

The rest of the plot of the lighting is contrast, color, and whether anyone else gets a face. It is the wrong tool to think of as a product.

You do not add a key on top of a finished picture. If two equally bright sources fight from opposite sides, you no longer have a key.

You have cross lighting or a flattened stand-off.

How it works

Pick one source and one side. Typical portrait keys sit 30 to 45 degrees off camera and above eye line; a split key sits at 90 degrees; a butterfly key sits on axis and high.

Hardness follows apparent size: a small distant lamp or noon sun cuts a sharp nose shadow; a large silk or bounce wraps. Color follows the story source: daylight 5600K, tungsten around 3200K, flame nearer 1800K.

Prompt: Strong directional key light on [Subject] from a single defined source, the brightest light in the frame, shadows placed as composition.

When to use it

Use it the moment you must say which direction the scene is lit from, for example a don in an office keyed from a high practical. Do not add a second equally bright key on the other cheek.

Compared with similar shots

Fill light only lifts what the key cannot reach. Hard light and soft light are qualities the key can have, not replacements for it.

Three-point lighting is a system that includes a key. Motivated lighting decides whether that key could exist in the room.

Fill LightControl how much of the dark you can still read.

Hard LightGrit, noon sun, or interrogation.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Godfather often lets a high, underexposed key leave eyes in wells of shadow. Apocalypse Now uses a hard, small key on faces so the jungle night stays black.

Those films treat the key as the sentence, not as one of three equal lamps.

Prompt it

Name the source and the side before any style word. " Add height (high, eye, table), hardness, and Kelvin.

If you only write dramatic lighting, the model invents two keys.

Use in Image Generator

Strong directional key light on [Subject] from a single defined source, the brightest storyteller in the frame, shadows as composition.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is fill bright enough to become a second key. The tell is two nose highlights and no clear shadow side.

Fix it by dimming or killing the fill until one direction owns exposure.

Questions

What is key light in film?

The principal light that defines the subject's dominant direction, shape, and exposure. Other lights are ratios against it.

Key light vs fill light

The key creates the shadow pattern. Fill reduces that contrast without inventing a second dominant direction.

When should I use key light?

Always, in the sense that every lit scene has a brightest story source. Name it first, then decide fill, back, and color.

How do I prompt key light for AI image or video?

State one source, one side, hardness, and color. Example: hard tungsten key from camera left, 45 degrees off axis, no second key.

entries.title: Fill Light
entries.text:
Fill Light

Fill light reduces contrast or adds detail in areas the key does not reach, usually from the opposite side and at a lower level. It is a ratio tool, not a second sun.

Create this Fill Light

Narrative function

In a scene fill decides how much of the dark you can still read: the far eye, the wall, a hand in a lap. A high fill ratio (close to the key) feels open and public.

A low fill ratio keeps mystery without crushing the face to a cut-out. It is the wrong tool when you want graphic black, or when bounce from the room already does the job.

Adding a frontal fill because a monitor looks noisy just flattens the key you spent an hour placing.

How it works

Put fill opposite the key, larger and softer than the key so it does not cast a competing nose shadow. Control it with distance, scrim, or dimmer; common portrait ratios run from about 2:1 (gentle) to 8:1 (lean).

Color is often a touch cooler or neutral versus a warm key so the shadow side does not go orange. Bounce off a wall can be the fill with no extra lamp.

Prompt: Soft fill light opening the shadow side of [Subject] without flattening, a low ratio that keeps eyes alive.

When to use it

Use it when a keyed close-up still needs the far iris and cheek pore, for example an interview after a hard window key. Do not pour fill in until both cheeks match.

Compared with similar shots

The key light sets direction; fill only answers it. Bounce light is a method that often becomes fill.

High-key lighting uses a lot of fill across the whole frame, not a single cheek opener. Eye light is smaller still: a catchlight, not a shadow-side wash.

Key LightDecide where the world is lit from. Everything else follows.

High-Key LightingComedy, heaven, hospital, or candy.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Classical portrait cinematography, including close-ups in Casablanca, keeps enough fill for both eyes without erasing the key. The Age of Innocence uses soft interior fill so period rooms stay readable while lamps still feel like the source.

Borrow the ratio, not the wallpaper.

Prompt it

Say which cheek opens and how little. " Add 2:1 or 4:1 if you need a number.

Do not ask for bright even light if you still want a key.

Use in Image Generator

Soft fill light opening the shadow side of [Subject] without flattening, a low ratio that keeps eyes alive.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a second key from camera right. The tell is a second nose shadow or a shadowless face.

Fix it by making fill larger, dimmer, and shadowless, or by bouncing it.

Questions

What is fill light in film?

Light that reduces contrast or adds detail where the key does not reach. It is dimmer and usually softer than the key.

Fill light vs bounce light

Fill is the job (open the shadows). Bounce is a method (reflect the key off a surface) that often performs that job.

When should I use fill light?

Use it when the keyed shadow side must stay readable. Skip it when the story wants deep, clean shadow.

How do I prompt fill light for AI image or video?

Name the shadow side and a low ratio. Example: soft fill on camera right, two stops under the key, eyes still visible, cheeks not even.

entries.title: Backlight
entries.text:
Backlight

hair light when on hairVolumetric shaftsLight beams in haze

Backlight in backlight cinematography is light coming from behind the subject toward the camera, tracing edges and lifting the figure off the background. It may stay a thin rim or, in haze, become a visible shaft.

Volume

Create this Backlight

Narrative function

A dark coat in a dark room disappears without an edge. Backlight draws that edge on hair, shoulders, and hat brim so the cutout reads.

In rain, dust, or smoke the same rear source can turn into volume, implying a world outside the frame: a searchlight, a high window, the sun. It is the wrong tool when you need the face, not the outline.

If you expose for the backlight, you get a silhouette. If you wrap it around to the cheek, you have started a kicker, not a true back.

How it works

Place the source behind and usually above, aimed toward camera, flagged so it does not flare unless you want veil. Hardness can be hard (sun, PAR, searchlight) for a sharp rim or softer for a glow in hair.

Color is often warmer than the key so the edge reads as sun or tungsten. Suspended particles make the beam itself photograph; without them you only see the rim on the body.

Prompt: Backlight on [Subject] from behind, rim of light tracing edges, slight veil, separation from background.

When to use it

Use it to separate a dark figure from a dark world, as in a smoky interior with one high window behind. Do not use it as the only light on a scene that still needs a face.

Compared with similar shots

Rim light is the thin highlight backlight can produce when tightly flagged. Kicker sits behind and to the side, kissing jaw or shoulder rather than wrapping the whole outline.

Silhouette exposes for the bright ground and lets the figure go black. Volumetric light needs haze so the beam, not just the rim, is visible.

Hair light is backlight aimed only at the hair.

Rim LightGraphic silhouette with just enough flesh.

SilhouetteIdentity is less important than shape.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Blade Runner cuts searchlights through smoky interiors so backlight becomes architecture. The Exorcist uses a powerful house light behind Merrin as he arrives.

Days of Heaven and Blade Runner 2049 keep the sun or a hard rear source as the edge that holds a figure in a bright or dusty ground.

Blade Runner 1982Searchlights and hard shafts cut through smoky interiors.

The Exorcist 1973Merrin arrives beneath the powerful light from the house.

Prompt it

Put the source behind the body, not on the nose. " Name hair, coat edge, and whether haze is present.

Do not ask for a glowing outline sticker.

Use in Video Generator

A conservator enters a dark archive where one high window sends a narrow hard shaft through suspended dust. Her body briefly interrupts the beam, producing a coherent moving shadow in the haze. Deep room, restrained atmosphere, no magical glowing particles.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a silhouette or a neon stroke. The tell is zero facial exposure, or a cartoon ring disconnected from any lamp.

Fix it by exposing a little of the key side and attaching the rim to a real rear source.

Questions

What is backlight in film?

Light from behind the subject toward the camera. It separates the figure with an edge, and in particles it can show a beam.

Backlight vs rim light

Backlight is the direction. Rim light is the narrow highlight that direction can paint on the outline when the source is flagged tight.

When should I use backlight?

Use it when a dark subject would otherwise merge with a dark background, or when a rear sun or window should halo the figure.

How do I prompt backlight for AI image or video?

Say the lamp or sun is behind the subject, name the edges that catch, and say whether the face stays dark. Add haze only if you want a visible shaft.

entries.title: Rim Light
entries.text:
Rim Light

Rim lighting is a narrow edge of light, usually from a flagged backlight, that separates a subject from the background without opening the face. The highlight sits on brim, hair, and coat; flesh stays mostly dark.

Create this Rim Light

Narrative function

The shot becomes a graphic: a profile or three-quarter figure drawn with a thread of exposure. You keep just enough flesh to know it is a person, not a paper doll.

Crime, spy, and night-city work use it so a body reads against wet asphalt or a black wall. It is the wrong tool for a dialogue close-up that needs both eyes.

If the rim fattens into a cheek slash, you have a kicker. If the whole figure goes empty and the sky is the subject, you have a silhouette.

How it works

Use a small hard source behind the subject, slightly off to one side, with flags or a snoot so the beam only kisses the outline. Keep it out of the lens unless you want veil.

Color is often white or slightly cool against a warmer dim key, or warm against night blue. Do not wrap to the front plane of the face.

Prompt: Photographic backlight on [Subject] from behind, a thin natural highlight on hat brim, hair, and coat edge, faces staying dark. Not a neon outline.

When to use it

Use it for a graphic night figure, a spy on a roof, a coat against a black street. Do not use it when the audience must read a mouth for a line.

Compared with similar shots

Backlight is the broader rear direction; rim is the thin result. Kicker hits cheek, jaw, or shoulder as a hard side-back accent with more flesh.

Hair light lights only the hair from above-behind. Silhouette removes the edge highlight and exposes for the ground instead.

BacklightSeparate a dark figure from a dark world.

KickerAdd a slice of glamour or menace on the far side.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Blade Runner rims figures in smoky interiors so coats and hair hold against black. Skyfall uses thin natural rims on night exteriors, faces kept dark, outlines readable.

Those are edges from sources, not stickers.

Prompt it

Forbid the cartoon stroke. Use: "Photographic backlight on [Subject] from behind, a thin natural highlight on hat brim, hair, and coat edge, faces staying dark.

" Name one rear lamp. Keep skin exposure low.

Use in Image Generator

Photographic backlight on [Subject] from behind, a thin natural highlight on hat brim, hair, and coat edge, faces staying dark. Not a neon outline.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a neon outline or a full silhouette. The tell is a glowing closed stroke around the body, or no highlight at all.

Fix it by attaching a thin highlight to hair and cloth only, from a real rear source.

Questions

What is rim light in film?

A narrow edge of light that separates the subject from the background. The face stays dark; brim, hair, and cloth catch the highlight.

Rim light vs kicker

A rim traces the outline. A kicker is a harder side-back slash on jaw, cheek, or shoulder, with more flesh in the accent.

When should I use rim light?

Use it when shape matters more than expression, and a dark figure must still unstick from a dark ground.

How do I prompt rim light for AI image or video?

Specify a thin natural highlight on hair and coat from behind, face remaining dark, no neon outline. Name the rear source.

entries.title: Kicker
entries.text:
Kicker

Kicker light

A kicker light is a relatively hard side-back accent on cheek, jaw, shoulder, or an object edge, placed behind and to one side of the subject. It is a slice, not a full wrap and not a hair-only rim.

Create this Kicker

Narrative function

The far plane of the face suddenly has a strip of glamour or menace. In noir it can be a streetlight kissing the jaw of someone who is otherwise in the key's shadow.

In a commercial portrait it is the same physics with a kinder color: a small lamp that says the cheek has a plane. It is the wrong tool if you need an even beauty wrap, or if the accent becomes a beam shooting out of the neck.

One kicker. If you add its twin on the other side you are in cross lighting.

How it works

Park a small hard source behind the subject, 30 to 60 degrees off the back axis, at about cheek height or a little above. Flag it off the camera and off the nose.

Hardness should be harder than the key so the accent is a clean line. Color is often a step warmer (tungsten, amber practical) against a cooler key, or white against tungsten.

Prompt: A small warm lamp behind and to the side of [Subject], a thin highlight on the far jaw and coat shoulder only. No beam shooting out of the body.

When to use it

Use it to add a slice of glamour or menace on the far side of a keyed face, for example a jawline in a night interior. Do not fire kickers from both sides unless you want a concert edge.

Compared with similar shots

Rim light traces the whole outline and leaves the cheek darker. Backlight sits more directly behind.

Hair light aims up at the hair, not the jaw. Side lighting keys the face from 90 degrees; a kicker does not become the key.

Rim LightGraphic silhouette with just enough flesh.

BacklightSeparate a dark figure from a dark world.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Film noir portraits, including work in the neighborhood of Double Indemnity and The Big Combo, use a hard far-side kicker on jaw and shoulder. Commercial portraiture borrowed the same accent with softer keys.

Treat those as a placement, not a costume.

Prompt it

Localize the highlight. Use: "A small warm lamp behind and to the side of [Subject], a thin highlight on the far jaw and coat shoulder only.

" Name left or right. Keep the key on the other side.

Use in Image Generator

A small warm lamp behind and to the side of [Subject], a thin highlight on the far jaw and coat shoulder only. No beam shooting out of the body.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a rim or a light saber from the neck. The tell is a closed outline, or a shaft growing out of the shoulder.

Fix it by shrinking the source, flagging it, and stopping the highlight on jaw and cloth.

Questions

What is a kicker in film?

A relatively hard side-back accent on cheek, jaw, shoulder, or object edge. It sits behind and to the side, and it is not the key.

Kicker vs rim light

A kicker is a localized slash of flesh and cloth. A rim is a thinner outline highlight that does not open the far cheek as much.

When should I use a kicker?

Use it when the far jaw or shoulder needs a hard accent of glamour or threat while the key still owns the face.

How do I prompt a kicker for AI image or video?

Place a small warm lamp behind and to one side. Limit the highlight to far jaw and shoulder. Forbid beams coming out of the body.

entries.title: Hair Light
entries.text:
Hair Light

A hair light is a small source behind and above the subject that lights only the top of the hair as a rim so texture separates from the background. The face stays on the key or in cooler shadow.

Create this Hair Light

Narrative function

Black hair, black wardrobe, black set: without a hair light the head becomes a hole. The unit is a separation tool, not a beauty wash.

Studio portraits and classical close-ups use it so a bun, a wave, or a wet scalp has a specular edge. It is the wrong tool when the story is a hat brim or a bald scalp you do not want to grease, or when a full backlight should wrap shoulders as well.

If the lamp drops to cheek height it becomes a kicker.

How it works

Mount a small lamp high and behind, slightly opposite the key, snooted or barred so it hits hair and maybe the top of the shoulders only. Hardness is usually harder than the key so strands sparkle.

Color is often a bit warmer than the face, or matching the key. Keep it out of the eyes.

Prompt: A small lamp behind and above [Subject], lighting only the top of the hair as a rim. The face stays in cooler shadow.

When to use it

Use it when dark hair would vanish into a dark wall, for example a brunette in a black interior. Do not use it as a ceiling wash that skims the forehead and noses.

Compared with similar shots

Backlight can include hair but also shoulders and veil. Rim light runs the whole outline.

Kicker kisses jaw, not the crown. Three-point lighting often uses a hair light as its back point.

Glam may include a hair edge, but glam is a frontal beauty package.

BacklightSeparate a dark figure from a dark world.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

Key LightDecide where the world is lit from. Everything else follows.

In film

Studio portraiture and classical close-ups, including blonde and brunette work in Gentlemen Prefer Blondes and the constructed hair edges in Vertigo, keep a small rear-top unit on the hair. The face still belongs to the key.

Prompt it

Aim at the crown, not the nose. Use: "A small lamp behind and above [Subject], lighting only the top of the hair as a rim.

" Name hair color so the model does not bleach the scalp.

Use in Image Generator

A small lamp behind and above [Subject], lighting only the top of the hair as a rim. The face stays in cooler shadow.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a full backlight or a halo. The tell is a glowing oval around the head, or forehead shine from above.

Fix it by snooting the unit onto hair only and keeping the face on the key.

Questions

What is a hair light in film?

A small lamp behind and above the subject that lights hair texture as a rim. It separates dark hair from a dark background without relighting the face.

Hair light vs backlight

A hair light is a restricted backlight aimed at the crown. Backlight may wrap the whole rear edge, including shoulders and atmosphere.

When should I use a hair light?

Use it when black or dark hair would merge with the set. Skip it on hats, bald heads you want matte, or when a full rear rim is the point.

How do I prompt a hair light for AI image or video?

Place a small lamp behind and above, lighting only the top of the hair. Keep the face in the key or in cooler shadow.

entries.title: Eye Light
entries.text:
Eye Light

An eye light in eye light cinematography is a small frontal source used to put a catchlight in the irises or to lift the eyes a fraction without becoming a fill. The face can stay in shadow; the eyes remain human, not lamps.

Create this Eye Light

Narrative function

A dark portrait dies if the sockets are empty pits with no specular. A tiny reflection of a lamp in each iris tells you there is a person looking.

Crime close-ups and night interrogations use it so the audience can track thought while the room stays black. It is the wrong tool when you need to open a whole cheek (that is fill) or when the character should feel blind, dead, or monstrous.

If the eyes glow, the model has turned the catchlight into an emitter.

How it works

Place a small, weak source near camera, often just above the lens, dim enough that it does not flatten the key's shadow pattern. A white card, a dim LED, or a distant practical can be enough.

Color is usually white or matching the key; keep it out of the skin as much as possible. You want a pinpoint in the iris, not a beauty wash.

Prompt: A dark portrait of [Subject], face mostly in shadow, a tiny white reflection of a lamp sitting in each human iris. Eyes stay brown or grey, not glowing.

When to use it

Use it to keep a soul in a dark portrait, for example a close-up where the key leaves the eyes in wells. Do not turn the pupils into light sources.

Compared with similar shots

Fill light opens the whole shadow cheek. Key light shapes the face.

Low-key lighting is the contrast environment that often needs an eye light. Top light without an eye light leaves sockets hollow on purpose.

Low-Key LightingMystery, crime, or moral night.

Key LightDecide where the world is lit from. Everything else follows.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Godfather sometimes withholds even this glint, which is why a tiny eye light in other Gordon Willis-adjacent close-ups feels like a choice. No Country for Old Men keeps dark rooms with human catchlights, not shining irises.

Use the physics: a reflection, not an emission.

Prompt it

Specify a reflection, not a glow. Use: "A dark portrait of [Subject], face mostly in shadow, a tiny white reflection of a lamp sitting in each human iris.

" Keep the key off-axis so the rest of the face stays dark.

Use in Image Generator

A dark portrait of [Subject], face mostly in shadow, a tiny white reflection of a lamp sitting in each human iris. Eyes stay brown or grey, not glowing.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is fill or supernatural glowing eyes. The tell is an opened face, or irises emitting light.

Fix it by dimming the frontal source to a catchlight and stating eye color as a surface.

Questions

What is an eye light in film?

A small frontal source that creates catchlights in the irises or slightly lifts the eyes. It does not relight the face.

Eye light vs fill light

Fill opens the shadow side of the whole face. An eye light is smaller and only puts a specular in the eyes, or a whisper of exposure there.

When should I use an eye light?

Use it in a dark portrait when the audience must still meet the gaze. Skip it when empty sockets are the point.

How do I prompt an eye light for AI image or video?

Describe a tiny white lamp reflection in each human iris, face remaining in shadow, eyes a natural brown or grey, not glowing.

entries.title: High-Key Lighting
entries.text:
High-Key Lighting

Low-contrast luminous lighting

High-key lighting, or high key lighting, uses relatively low contrast, bright exposure, and limited deep shadow so the frame stays open and readable. It is a contrast ratio, not a command to overexpose.

Volume

Create this High-Key Lighting

Narrative function

Comedy, heaven, hospital, and candy shops live here because the world looks safe, clean, or artificially perfect. Strong colors can still sit in a high-key frame; the shadows simply do not go to black.

A sour performance inside that brightness can also prove the promise is false. It is the wrong tool for crime, night, or any beat that needs a hiding place.

Bright is not the same as blown. If every surface is the same white, you lost material and face.

How it works

Use large sources, plenty of fill, and often bounce from walls and ceiling so the ratio sits near 2:1 or lower. Key can still have a side; it is just not a cliff.

Protect highlight detail on skin, icing, walls. Color is often daylight-balanced or pastel-friendly, sometimes slightly cool for sterile spaces, sometimes candy-warm.

Prompt: High-key lighting on [Subject], bright even illumination, minimal shadows, airy overexposure by a third, optimism or sterile future.

When to use it

Use it for a comic interior, a showroom, a hospital, or a toy world that should feel open. Do not use it as a synonym for overexposure, and do not use it on a murder scene unless you want irony.

Compared with similar shots

Low-key lighting is the opposite ratio: selective light and substantial shadow. Soft light is hardness; you can have soft low-key.

Glam sells a face with a large key but can still sit in a contrasty room. Cameo lighting isolates a figure in black, the reverse of an open high-key world.

Soft LightBeauty, memory, or kindness.

Low-Key LightingMystery, crime, or moral night.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Umbrellas of Cherbourg keeps brightly colored interiors openly lit so romance is artificial and clear. Barbie builds Barbieland as a carefully controlled bright world with preserved highlight detail.

2001: A Space Odyssey uses high-key Discovery spaces that stay clean rather than crushed. Marie Antoinette often lives in luminous rooms.

The Umbrellas of Cherbourg 1964Brightly colored interiors sustain an openly artificial romantic world.

Barbie 2023The bright, carefully controlled world of Barbieland.

Prompt it

Ask for low contrast and protected whites, not a flash. " Add large sources and say highlights hold texture.

Avoid calling it low-key just because the genre is serious.

Use in Video Generator

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is overexposure or soft light in a dark room. The tell is clipped walls, or a bright face in a black void (cameo).

Fix it by lowering contrast across the whole set and holding highlight detail.

Questions

What is high-key lighting in film?

A low-contrast, bright setup with limited deep shadow. The scene can still have color and some modeling; it is not automatically overexposed.

High-key lighting vs low-key lighting

High-key keeps the frame open and the ratio low. Low-key uses high contrast and lets most of the frame fall into shadow.

When should I use high-key lighting?

Use it for comedy, sterile spaces, showrooms, or candy-bright worlds. Do not use it when darkness must hide information.

How do I prompt high-key lighting for AI image or video?

Specify bright even illumination, minimal shadows, large sources, and highlight texture preserved. Say overexposure by no more than a third.

entries.title: Low-Key Lighting
entries.text:
Low-Key Lighting

Low-key lighting, or low key lighting, uses high contrast, selective illumination, and substantial shadow so most of the frame can sit near black. One pool of light is often enough; the dark is designed, not an accident of underexposure.

Create this Low-Key Lighting

Narrative function

Mystery, crime, and moral night live here because the audience cannot see the whole room. A face, a gun, a doorway gets the pool; the rest is withheld.

The ratio is the story: who is visible, who is not. It is the wrong tool for comedy timing that needs both eyes, or for a location you must geography-read.

Diming a fully lit office until it is muddy is not low-key. That is just a dark even room.

How it works

Place a motivated key, kill bounce with flags and black wrap, and keep fill several stops down (often 8:1 or more). Hardness is frequently hard so shadow edges stay graphic, but soft low-key exists if the source is large and still isolated.

Color is often tungsten in a black room, or a single cool slash. Prompt: Low-key lighting on [Subject], most of the frame in deep shadow, one pool of light, 8:1 contrast, darkness as a designed space.

When to use it

Use it for a crime close-up, a night office, a corridor with one practical. Do not underexpose an evenly lit room and call it low-key.

Compared with similar shots

Chiaroscuro is low-key used to model volume with a painter's moral contrast; not every low-key frame is chiaroscuro. Hard light often serves low-key but is a quality, not the ratio.

High-key lighting is the opposite. Cameo lighting erases the environment entirely; low-key can still imply a room in the dark.

ChiaroscuroLight is moral. Darkness hides or judges.

Hard LightGrit, noon sun, or interrogation.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Godfather keeps offices in selective pools against the bright wedding outside. The Big Combo and Se7en use high-contrast night as a working space, not a grade slapped on a bright master.

Borrow the pool and the flags, not a grain preset.

Prompt it

Name the pool and the black. " Name the single source and forbid extra fill.

Do not write moody if you have not placed the lamp.

Use in Image Generator

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a dark high-key (everything dimmed equally) or crushed blacks with no face. The tell is no key direction.

Fix it by placing one source and flagging spill, then exposing for that pool.

Questions

What is low-key lighting in film?

A high-contrast setup with selective illumination and substantial shadow. Darkness is shaped, not merely underexposed.

Low-key lighting vs chiaroscuro

Low-key is the contrast strategy. Chiaroscuro uses that contrast to model volume and often a moral split between light and dark.

When should I use low-key lighting?

Use it for mystery, crime, or any night that should withhold space. Do not use it when the geography of the room is the joke or the plot.

How do I prompt low-key lighting for AI image or video?

Put most of the frame in deep shadow, name one pool of light, and state a high ratio such as 8:1. Name the single source.

entries.title: Chiaroscuro
entries.text:
Chiaroscuro

Selective darknessClair-obscur

Chiaroscuro lighting uses strong light-dark contrast to model volume and to create moral, psychological, or dramatic tension. Darkness withholds; the lit plane is what the scene will admit.

Volume

Create this Chiaroscuro

Narrative function

A single warm source, a face turning into light, the rest of the room falling away: the audience reads character as a matter of what remains visible. Tenebrism is the hard end of this, where everything beyond arm's reach is black.

Crime, period night, and religious doubt all use the same physics. It is the wrong tool for a wide that must describe architecture, or for comedy that needs a second face in the shadows.

Underexposing an even room is not chiaroscuro. You have to place a key and let falloff do the cutting.

How it works

Place one motivated key (window, lamp, candle), reduce fill, and flag spill. The key is often warm, slightly high, and small enough to fall off fast.

Hardness can be moderately hard so planes of the face turn quickly. Keep enough separation that eyes and hands in the pool stay legible.

Prompt: Chiaroscuro lighting on [Subject], Caravaggio tenebrism, a single warm source, everything beyond arm's reach falling into black.

When to use it

Use it when light is moral and darkness hides or judges, for example a confession across a desk lamp. Do not use it as a global grade on a daylight street.

Compared with similar shots

Low-key lighting is the broader contrast strategy; chiaroscuro insists on modeled volume, not just a dark frame. Rembrandt lighting is a specific cheek-triangle pattern that often lives inside chiaroscuro.

Cameo lighting isolates against void and may flatten the world to a stage cutout. Hard light helps the cut but is not required if falloff is steep.

Low-Key LightingMystery, crime, or moral night.

Rembrandt LightingClassic dramatic portrait.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Godfather's dark office against the wedding outside is textbook withholding. The Third Man uses Vienna night so figures appear and vanish in designed dark.

Barry Lyndon and The Night of the Hunter both let a single source model faces while the room dies.

The Godfather 1972The Don’s dark office contrasts with the wedding outside.

The Third Man 1949Vienna’s night streets and hidden figures.

Prompt it

One source, fast falloff, modeled planes. " Name the lamp.

Forbid extra fill and even ambient.

Use in Video Generator

A tailor listens to an uneasy visitor in a dim back room. One high window shapes half the tailor’s face; the rest falls into deep but readable shadow. Warm desk practical in the distance, no even beauty fill, no crushed featureless blacks.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is muddy underexposure. The tell is no key direction and featureless blacks.

Fix it by placing one warm source, flagging bounce, and exposing the lit planes.

Questions

What is chiaroscuro in film?

Strong light-dark contrast used to model volume and to create tension. Selected areas are lit; substantial parts of the image stay dark on purpose.

Chiaroscuro vs Rembrandt lighting

Chiaroscuro is the overall contrast language. Rembrandt lighting is a portrait pattern: a triangle of light on the shadow-side cheek.

When should I use chiaroscuro?

Use it when what is hidden matters as much as what is shown: confession, crime, night bargains. Skip it when the whole room must read.

How do I prompt chiaroscuro for AI image or video?

Specify a single warm source, faces modeled, everything beyond arm's reach falling into black. No extra fill, no even room tone.

entries.title: Rembrandt Lighting
entries.text:
Rembrandt Lighting

Rembrandt lighting, in rembrandt lighting terms, is a portrait pattern in which the key sits high and about 45 degrees off axis so the nose shadow joins the shadow cheek, leaving a small triangle of light under the shadow-side eye. The rest of that cheek stays dark.

Create this Rembrandt Lighting

Narrative function

The face becomes a painting with one lit plane and a pocket of light that proves the far eye still exists. Drama likes it because the head has volume without the graphic half-and-half of a split.

Period interiors and serious close-ups use it when the key could be a high window or a lamp. It is the wrong tool for a beauty close-up that should open both cheeks evenly, or for a character you want fully public.

If the nose shadow does not connect to the cheek shadow, you have loop lighting, not Rembrandt.

How it works

Put a moderately hard or softly hard key high and roughly 45 degrees to one side, high enough that the nose shadow falls down and across until it meets the cheek shadow. The triangle sits below the far eye and should not spill across the whole far cheek.

Fill is low or absent. Color follows the source: warm interior, cooler window.

Short lighting (key on the far cheek) is the usual pairing. Prompt: Key light high and 45 degrees on [Subject], the near cheek in light, a small triangle of light on the shadow-side cheek, the rest of that cheek dark.

When to use it

Use it for a classic dramatic portrait, a period close-up, a bargainer across a table. Do not use it when you need an even glamour wrap or a literal half-lit mask.

Compared with similar shots

Loop lighting makes a small nose shadow that does not connect to the cheek shadow. Split lighting keys at 90 degrees and divides the face in half with no triangle.

Butterfly lighting puts the key on axis, high, with a shadow under the nose, both cheeks open. Chiaroscuro is the larger contrast language this pattern often sits in.

Bounce light would wrap the triangle away. Motivated lighting can create Rembrandt if the window sits in that high 45, but motivated is a justification, not this pattern.

Loop LightingNatural portrait that is still shaped.

ChiaroscuroLight is moral. Darkness hides or judges.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Fanny and Alexander uses painterly window keys that often land in this triangle. Road to Perdition, with Conrad Hall's portrait work, leans on Rembrandt-like faces in dark interiors.

Use the cheek geometry, not a still to duplicate.

Prompt it

Demand the triangle by name. " Say the nose shadow connects to the cheek shadow.

Forbid a half-and-half split.

Use in Image Generator

Key light high and 45 degrees on [Subject], the near cheek in light, a small triangle of light on the shadow-side cheek, the rest of that cheek dark.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is loop or split. The tell is a floating nose comma that never meets the cheek, or a face divided down the center with no triangle.

Fix it by raising and swinging the key until the shadows join, leaving a small lit triangle under the far eye.

Questions

What is Rembrandt lighting in film?

A portrait setup with the key high and about 45 degrees off axis so a triangle of light appears on the shadow-side cheek under the eye.

Rembrandt lighting vs loop lighting

In loop, the nose shadow is a small loop that does not touch the cheek shadow. In Rembrandt, that shadow connects, isolating a triangle of light on the far cheek.

When should I use Rembrandt lighting?

Use it for a dramatic portrait that still shows both eyes, one in a pocket of light. Skip it for glamour evenness or a literal split face.

How do I prompt Rembrandt lighting for AI image or video?

Place the key high and 45 degrees off axis. Specify a small triangle of light on the shadow-side cheek, the rest of that cheek dark, nose shadow connected.

entries.title: Butterfly Lighting
entries.text:
Butterfly Lighting

Paramount lighting

Butterfly lighting, also called Paramount lighting, places the key high and on the camera axis so a small butterfly-shaped shadow falls under the nose on the philtrum. Both cheeks stay open; both eyes take light.

Create this Butterfly Lighting

Narrative function

This is beauty lighting with a structure: cheekbones lift, the nose has a tidy shadow, and the face stays symmetrical for the lens. Classical glamour portraits used it because a star looking into camera still has modeling, not a flat flash.

It is the wrong tool for a liar in half-light, a bruised antihero, or anyone whose story is asymmetry. If you swing the key off axis, the butterfly becomes a loop.

If you raise it to the ceiling and kill the frontal component, you get top light sockets.

How it works

Center a large or medium source above the lens, aimed down at the face, high enough for the under-nose shadow but not so high the eye sockets collapse. A reflector under the chin is optional fill.

Hardness is usually soft to medium so skin wraps. Color is often tungsten or daylight beauty-neutral, not a green overhead.

Prompt: Key light high and centered on [Subject]'s face, a small shadow under the nose on the philtrum, both eyes open, glamour portrait.

When to use it

Use it for a glamour close-up, a singer facing camera, a studio beauty still. Do not use it on a crime profile that should be short-lit.

Compared with similar shots

Loop lighting moves the key slightly off axis so the nose shadow slides toward the mouth corner. Rembrandt lighting is further off and higher, with a cheek triangle.

Glam is the broader beauty package (diffusion, catchlights) that often uses butterfly but does not have to. High-key lighting is frame contrast, not this nose-shadow pattern.

Top light is overhead enough to bury the eyes.

Loop LightingNatural portrait that is still shaped.

High-Key LightingComedy, heaven, hospital, or candy.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Classic Hollywood glamour, including Paramount-style portraits and films such as Gilda and Shanghai Express, parks the key high and frontal so the butterfly sits under the nose. The face stays a product the camera can sell.

Prompt it

Keep the key on center and high. " Forbid a shadow cheek.

Mention both eyes taking light.

Use in Image Generator

Key light high and centered on [Subject]'s face, a small shadow under the nose on the philtrum, both eyes open, glamour portrait.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is loop or top light. The tell is a nose shadow that leans to one side, or hollow eyes.

Fix it by centering the key and lowering it until sockets open and the butterfly sits on the philtrum.

Questions

What is butterfly lighting in film?

A high, on-axis key that throws a small butterfly-shaped shadow under the nose. Both cheeks and both eyes stay lit. It is also called Paramount lighting.

Butterfly lighting vs loop lighting

Butterfly keeps the key centered; the nose shadow sits under the septum. Loop offsets the key so the shadow becomes a small loop toward the mouth, still not touching the cheek shadow.

When should I use butterfly lighting?

Use it for glamour and frontal beauty with a little structure. Skip it when the face should be secretive or half in shadow.

How do I prompt butterfly lighting for AI image or video?

Put the key high and centered. Ask for a small shadow under the nose on the philtrum, both eyes open, both cheeks lit.

entries.title: Loop Lighting
entries.text:
Loop Lighting

Loop lighting creates a small nose shadow that loops toward the corner of the mouth and does not connect to the cheek shadow. The key sits slightly off axis and a little high, a middle step between butterfly and Rembrandt.

Create this Loop Lighting

Narrative function

The face is shaped but still friendly: interviews, earnest close-ups, people we are supposed to trust. You get a hint of cheek shadow and a definite nose, without the painterly triangle or the glamour butterfly.

It is the wrong tool when you need a mask of light and dark, or a fashion-symmetric face. If that loop grows until it joins the cheek, you have crossed into Rembrandt.

If you center the key, you are back at butterfly.

How it works

Offset the key about 30 to 45 degrees from the nose, slightly above eye line, softness medium so the loop is a clean comma, not a smear. Fill can sit opposite at a gentle ratio (2:1 to 4:1).

Color is usually the room: window daylight or soft tungsten. The shadow-side cheek still receives some light; that is the difference from Rembrandt.

Prompt: Loop lighting on [Subject], key slightly off-axis, a small loop shadow from the nose toward the corner of the mouth.

When to use it

Use it for a natural portrait that is still shaped, an interview, a two-shot that should not look lit. Do not use it when you want a cheek triangle or a half-face cut.

Compared with similar shots

Rembrandt lighting connects nose shadow to cheek shadow and leaves a triangle. Butterfly lighting is on axis with a philtrum butterfly.

Split lighting goes to 90 degrees and drops the far cheek. Bounce will wrap the loop away if the source gets too large.

Motivated lighting may produce a loop from a slightly off window, but the pattern is the geometry, not the justification.

Rembrandt LightingClassic dramatic portrait.

Butterfly LightingBeauty lighting with structure.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Interview cinematography and news-adjacent films such as Frost/Nixon live on loop because both eyes stay open and the face still has a side. The Social Network's talking-head grammar often sits here: slightly off keys, not painterly triangles.

Prompt it

Name the loop and forbid the triangle. Use: "Loop lighting on [Subject], key slightly off-axis, a small loop shadow from the nose toward the corner of the mouth." Add that the loop does not touch the cheek shadow.

Use in Image Generator

Loop lighting on [Subject], key slightly off-axis, a small loop shadow from the nose toward the corner of the mouth.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Rembrandt or butterfly. The tell is a connected cheek triangle, or a perfectly centered under-nose butterfly.

Fix it by offsetting the key a little and stopping before the shadows merge.

Questions

What is loop lighting in film?

A slightly off-axis key that throws a small loop-shaped nose shadow toward the mouth corner. That shadow does not join the cheek shadow.

Loop lighting vs Rembrandt lighting

Loop leaves a gap between nose shadow and cheek shadow. Rembrandt joins them, creating a triangle of light on the far cheek.

When should I use loop lighting?

Use it for a natural, still-shaped portrait or interview. Skip it when you want glamour symmetry or a dramatic cheek triangle.

How do I prompt loop lighting for AI image or video?

entries.title: Split Lighting
entries.text:
Split Lighting

Split lighting divides the face into a lit half and a shadow half by placing the key at about 90 degrees to the nose, a vertical cut down the center line. There is no Rembrandt triangle and no loop; the far plane is largely gone.

Create this Split Lighting

Narrative function

Duality made as geometry: hero and liar, cop and crook, the same person cut in two. The audience gets one eye in light and one in almost nothing.

Music, crime, and moral argument use it because the cut is literal. It is the wrong tool for charm, romance, or any beat that needs both cheeks.

If you sneak fill across the center line, the split collapses into side lighting with wrap. If you raise the key and pull it forward, you may accidentally make Rembrandt.

How it works

Put a relatively hard key at 90 degrees to the face, at about eye height, so the shadow edge runs down forehead, nose, and chin. Fill is near zero.

Color can be a hard white or a theatrical gel; the point is the cut, not prettiness. A true split is more severe than generic side light because the wrap over the nose is killed with flags if needed.

Prompt: Split lighting on [Subject], one half of the face in light, the other in shadow, a vertical moral cut.

When to use it

Use it when a character is two things at once, a drummer under a side spot, a don in profile thought. Do not use it on a first-date close-up unless you want threat.

Compared with similar shots

Side lighting is the broader 90-degree direction and can still wrap a body or a room. Split is the facial pattern with a hard center line.

Rembrandt lighting keeps a triangle on the dark cheek; split does not. Loop lighting is much more frontal.

Short lighting can include a split if the dark cheek faces camera, but short is about which cheek the camera sees, not the 90-degree cut. Butterfly is the opposite: both cheeks open.

Side LightingCarve a face like sculpture.

Short LightingSculpt a face; add mystery on the camera side.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Godfather uses half-lit faces in the office so thought reads as a cut. Whiplash slashes players with hard side spots that often split the face on stage.

The pattern is the center line, not a mood word.

Prompt it

Demand the vertical cut. Use: "Split lighting on [Subject], one half of the face in light, the other in shadow, a vertical moral cut." Add key at 90 degrees, almost no fill, no triangle on the dark cheek.

Use in Image Generator

Split lighting on [Subject], one half of the face in light, the other in shadow, a vertical moral cut.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Rembrandt or wrapped side lighting. The tell is a pocket of light on the dark cheek, or a soft wrap over the nose.

Fix it by moving the key to 90 degrees and killing fill until the center line is clean.

Questions

What is split lighting in film?

A key at about 90 degrees that lights one half of the face and leaves the other in shadow. The cut runs vertically down the center of the face.

Split lighting vs Rembrandt lighting

Split has no triangle on the dark cheek; that half is gone. Rembrandt keeps a small triangle of light under the shadow-side eye.

When should I use split lighting?

Use it for duality, interrogation, or a theatrical side spot. Skip it when both eyes and both cheeks must sell a line.

How do I prompt split lighting for AI image or video?

Place the key at 90 degrees. State one half of the face in light, the other in shadow, no fill, no Rembrandt triangle.

entries.title: Short Lighting
entries.text:
Short Lighting

Short lighting in short lighting terms keys the side of the face turned away from camera, so the camera sees more shadow than light. The head looks slimmer and more dimensional because the near cheek falls off.

Create this Short Lighting

Narrative function

Mystery sits on the camera side. We look at the dark plane and infer the person from the far, lit cheek.

Noir portraits and serious close-ups use it so a face is sculpted instead of presented like a passport photo. It is the wrong tool when a comic or public figure should feel open to us.

Short is not a shadow pattern by itself: you can light short as Rembrandt, loop, or even a soft wrap. The definition is which cheek faces the lens, not the nose shadow.

How it works

Turn the face so the far cheek takes the key (often 45 to 90 degrees from camera). The near cheek, the one occupying more of the frame, goes toward shadow.

Hardness can be hard for noir or medium for drama. Color follows the key source.

Combine with a low fill so the near eye does not die unless you want it to. Prompt: Short lighting on [Subject], the side turned away from camera is keyed, the near side falls toward shadow, slimming and dramatic.

When to use it

Use it to sculpt a face and put mystery on the camera side, a close-up in an office or a night bar. Do not use it when the character is presenting themselves to the public in a broad, open way.

Compared with similar shots

Broad lighting keys the camera-facing cheek, the reverse. Rembrandt lighting is a triangle pattern often shot short, but Rembrandt can be broad if the triangle is on the near cheek.

Split lighting is a 90-degree cut that is usually short if the dark half faces us. Side lighting describes direction, not which cheek is near camera.

Broad LightingOpen, readable, less mystery.

Rembrandt LightingClassic dramatic portrait.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Portrait noir and Godfather-adjacent close-ups often key the far cheek so the camera sits with the shadow. Road to Perdition does the same sculpting in dark interiors.

Read the near cheek: if it is the dark one, you are short.

Prompt it

Name which cheek is near. Use: "Short lighting on [Subject], the side turned away from camera is keyed, the near side falls toward shadow, slimming and dramatic." Add that the camera-facing cheek is the darker one.

Use in Image Generator

Short lighting on [Subject], the side turned away from camera is keyed, the near side falls toward shadow, slimming and dramatic.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is broad lighting or a frontal butterfly. The tell is a bright near cheek filling the frame.

Fix it by turning the face or swinging the key onto the far side.

Questions

What is short lighting in film?

Lighting the side of the face turned away from camera so the near, camera-facing cheek falls toward shadow. It slims and adds dimension.

Short lighting vs broad lighting

Short keys the far cheek; the camera sees more shadow. Broad keys the near cheek; the camera sees more light.

When should I use short lighting?

Use it to sculpt a face and keep mystery on the camera side. Skip it for open, public, comic portraits.

How do I prompt short lighting for AI image or video?

State that the side turned away from camera is keyed and the near cheek falls toward shadow. Mention a slimming, dimensional face.

entries.title: Broad Lighting
entries.text:
Broad Lighting

Broad lighting keys the side of the face turned toward camera, so the near cheek is the bright one and the shadow sits on the far side. The face reads open, public, and less mysterious.

Create this Broad Lighting

Narrative function

Someone is presenting themselves: a speech, a studio comic, a star who must be fully available to the lens. The camera-facing plane carries the exposure, so pores and expression on that cheek are easy to read.

It is the wrong tool for menace, secrecy, or a slimming portrait on a wide face. Broad is not high-key; you can still have a dark room.

The definition is only which cheek is near and lit.

How it works

Turn the face or swing the key so the camera-facing cheek takes the key, often 30 to 45 degrees off a near-frontal axis. Fill can be generous.

Hardness is often softer than noir short lighting. Color is whatever the public space is: daylight, studio tungsten, a bright practical.

Prompt: Broad lighting on [Subject], the camera-facing side keyed, open and public, less shadow on the near cheek.

When to use it

Use it for an open, readable portrait, a public figure, a comic close-up. Do not use it when the near cheek should be the secret.

Compared with similar shots

Short lighting is the reverse: far cheek keyed, near cheek dark. High-key lighting is overall contrast, which often pairs with broad but is not the same job.

Butterfly lighting is on-axis, so neither cheek is favored. Loop lighting can be executed broad or short depending on head turn.

Short LightingSculpt a face; add mystery on the camera side.

High-Key LightingComedy, heaven, hospital, or candy.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Classical portraiture and studio comedy close-ups, including open faces in Roman Holiday and Singin' in the Rain, key the near cheek so the public can have the person. The shadow, if any, lives on the far side.

Prompt it

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is short lighting. The tell is a dark near cheek and a bright far sliver.

Fix it by turning the key onto the camera-facing side or turning the face toward the key.

Questions

What is broad lighting in film?

Lighting the side of the face turned toward camera. The near cheek is bright; the shadow sits farther away.

Broad lighting vs short lighting

Broad keys the near cheek and feels open. Short keys the far cheek and puts mystery on the camera side.

When should I use broad lighting?

Use it when a face should feel public and easy to read. Skip it when you want sculpture and withheld information.

entries.title: Silhouette
entries.text:
Silhouette

Shape-led compositionOmbre chinoise

A silhouette shot places the subject dark against a brighter background so the figure reads as shape, not as a modeled face. Gesture and contour do the work; surface detail is gone.

Volume

Create this Silhouette

Narrative function

Identity is less important than emblem: a rider on a ridge, a bicycle against a moon, a man in a doorway. The audience recognizes an action from outline alone.

If two shapes merge, the sentence is lost. It is the wrong tool when a line of dialogue needs a mouth, or when you still want pores and color in the coat.

A little rim is not a silhouette. If you can name the eye color, you overexposed the figure.

How it works

Expose for the bright ground (sky, doorway, fire, sun disk). Keep the key off the subject, or far below the background.

Backlight may exist as a sky, not as a facial key. Separate limbs, hats, and props so the outline parses.

Hardness of the background source can be hard sun or a bright overcast; the subject is simply underexposed. Prompt: Silhouette of [Subject] as a dark shape against a bright ground, surface detail gone, mythic outline only.

When to use it

Use it when identity matters less than shape, a departure through a door, a figure against dusk. Do not use it if the action cannot be read from the outline.

Compared with similar shots

Backlight can create a silhouette if you expose for it, or a rim if you hold the face a little. Rim light keeps a thread of flesh highlight; silhouette usually does not.

Cameo lighting is the inverse: a lit figure on a black ground. Low-key lighting still models something in the pool.

BacklightSeparate a dark figure from a dark world.

Rim LightGraphic silhouette with just enough flesh.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

T. the Extra-Terrestrial puts bicycle and riders in silhouette across the moon.

The Searchers isolates a figure against a bright doorway and landscape. Lawrence of Arabia and Skyfall use desert and sun as the bright field that turns bodies into emblems.

E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial 1982The bicycle and riders pass in silhouette across the moon.

The Searchers 1956The figure is isolated against the bright doorway and landscape.

Prompt it

Expose the ground, starve the body. " Name a readable outline (limbs separated).

Forbid facial detail and neon rims.

Use in Video Generator

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a rim portrait or a muddy underexposure on a dark ground. The tell is visible eyes, or a black figure on a black field.

Fix it by brightening the background, killing keys on the body, and separating the limbs.

Questions

What is a silhouette in film?

A subject placed dark against a brighter background so contour and gesture read instead of facial detail.

Silhouette vs rim light

A silhouette is an unmodeled dark shape on a bright field. Rim light keeps a thin highlight on the edge of a still-dark figure, often on a dark field.

When should I use a silhouette?

Use it when the outline is the sentence: departure, arrival, emblem. Skip it when the face must speak.

How do I prompt a silhouette for AI image or video?

Ask for a dark shape against a bright ground, no surface detail, limbs separated. Expose for the sky or doorway, not the face.

entries.title: Motivated Lighting
entries.text:
Motivated Lighting

Music source revealSource-score play

Motivated lighting is designed to appear consistent with a visible or plausible story-world source: a window, a lamp, a sign, the sky. Hidden units may exist, but they match that source in direction, hardness, and color.

Create this Motivated Lighting

Narrative function

The room feels like a world rather than a studio. A hotel sconce, a kitchen window, a sodium street, an overcast sky: the key could have come from there even if a silk outside the window is doing the real work.

Control stays; theatricality hides. It is the wrong tool when the point is frankly theatrical (a follow spot, a beauty butterfly that no lamp in the room could throw).

Motivated is not the same as using only what is already there. That is available light.

It is also not the same as showing the bulb. That is a practical.

How it works

Choose the story source first. Match camera-side direction to that window or fixture.

Match hardness: a distant sun stays hard; a sheer curtain becomes a large soft key; a bare bulb stays small. Match color: tungsten practicals around 2800 to 3200K, daylight windows nearer 5600K, sodium and neon as they are.

Hide extra units along the same axis, flagged to the same throw. Prompt: Motivated lighting on [Subject], every source justified by a window, lamp, or sign that could exist in the room.

When to use it

Use it for realism with control, a hotel corridor, a kitchen at 4 p.m., a car at night that should feel streetlit. Do not use it as an excuse to keep a frontal beauty key that no source in the space could explain.

Compared with similar shots

Practical lighting is the visible fixture in frame; motivated lighting can boost or replace it from hiding. Available light uses what exists without adding units.

Naturalistic ambient is the overall wrap that hides craft. Bounce light is a method you may use to imitate a wall or ceiling the story already has.

Rembrandt and window light are patterns or sources that motivated work often chooses, not synonyms.

Practical LightingLet the set light the face.

Available LightCommit to the hour you have.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Shining lets lamps and hotel fixtures justify interior direction. Children of Men keeps windows, fixtures, and available sky as the logic of the frame.

Blade Runner 2049 and In the Mood for Love build rooms whose keys could be the signs, blinds, and lamps we see, even when film lights help.

Blazing Saddles 1974A seemingly conventional musical accompaniment is revealed as a band in the desert.

Birdman 2014Visible percussion performance plays with the status of the drum soundtrack.

Yi Yi 2000The image eventually identifies the source of previously heard piano music.

The Shining 1980Lamps and hotel fixtures motivate much of the interior look.

Children of Men 2006Windows, fixtures and available light help maintain a grounded world.

Prompt it

Justify every beam. " Name the story source, its side, hardness, and Kelvin.

Forbid an unexplained frontal beauty key.

Use in Video Generator

A solemn traveler crosses an empty plaza accompanied by an original elegant string theme. Pan slowly to reveal a small string quartet following him on a wheeled platform, still playing the exact phrase. Their presence is treated matter-of-factly. Generate the visual reveal and synchronize an original performance in the edit.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is unmotivated studio three-point or claiming available light while describing movie lamps. The tell is a key from a wall with no window or fixture.

Fix it by naming the story source and aligning hidden units to it.

Questions

What is motivated lighting in film?

Lighting designed to look as if it comes from a plausible story-world source. Extra units are allowed if they match that source's direction, hardness, and color.

Motivated lighting vs practical lighting

A practical is a visible lamp in the set. Motivated lighting is the logic: hidden lights may imitate or reinforce that lamp or a window you may not even see.

When should I use motivated lighting?

Use it when the scene should feel like a real room with control. Skip it for frankly theatrical spots and beauty setups the room cannot explain.

How do I prompt motivated lighting for AI image or video?

Name the window, lamp, or sign that justifies every source. Match direction, hardness, and color to that object. No orphan movie lights.

entries.title: Practical Lighting
entries.text:
Practical Lighting

Practical lighting uses a visible or logically present light source within the set as a real contributor: lamps, neon, candles, screens. You see the fixture, and it (or a unit matching it) actually lights the face.

Volume

Create this Practical Lighting

Narrative function

The set becomes the lighting department. A table lamp in the foreground, a TV, a diner sign: the audience believes the room because the source is in the shot.

Mixed color temperatures are a feature, not a mistake. It is the wrong tool when the fixture is only set dressing and a frontal key from nowhere does the work.

A dark lamp in frame with a face lit from camera is a lie. If the lamp is off-screen but implied, you have shifted toward motivated lighting.

How it works

Put working fixtures in frame, often brighter than a real living room so they expose on camera. Control them with bulbs, dimmers, and flags.

Hardness is whatever the shade allows: a bare bulb is hard; a cloth shade is softer. Color is mixed on purpose: tungsten 2700 to 3200K, neon magenta or cyan, screens cooler.

You may hide a small unit in the same shade. Prompt: Practical lighting on [Subject] from visible lamps, neon, candles, or screens in frame, mixed color temperatures, no hidden movie lights.

When to use it

Use it when the set should light the face, a night apartment, a bar, a car dash. Do not leave dead props in frame while a beauty key does the real job.

Compared with similar shots

Motivated lighting can hide units that match a source; practicals are the sources you see. Candlelight is a specific small warm practical with fast falloff.

Neon practicals are a color-and-sign subset. Available light might include existing fixtures but forbids adding them.

Window light is often a practical architecture plus sky.

Motivated LightingRealism with control. Light like a world, not a studio.

CandlelightPeriod night or ritual.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Barry Lyndon puts flame in frame as the logic of night. In the Mood for Love and Blade Runner 2049 let lamps, neon, and screens in the set do visible work on faces.

The fixture is part of the composition, not only the plot.

Prompt it

Show the lamp and let it work. Use: "Practical lighting on [Subject] from visible lamps, neon, candles, or screens in frame, mixed color temperatures, no hidden movie lights." Name which fixture is the key and its color.

Use in Image Generator

Practical lighting on [Subject] from visible lamps, neon, candles, or screens in frame, mixed color temperatures, no hidden movie lights.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a dummy lamp plus an off-screen key. The tell is a dark shade and a face lit from the camera.

Fix it by turning the practical up (or matching a hidden unit inside it) and killing the orphan frontal.

Questions

What is practical lighting in film?

Using visible set fixtures as real lights: lamps, neon, candles, screens. The source is in the world of the shot and it contributes exposure.

Practical lighting vs motivated lighting

Practicals are the fixtures you see. Motivated lighting is the matching logic, which can include hidden units that imitate a window or lamp.

When should I use practical lighting?

Use it when the room should visibly light the people. Skip dummy lamps that do not expose.

How do I prompt practical lighting for AI image or video?

Name visible lamps, neon, candles, or screens as the keys, mixed color temperatures, no hidden movie lights. Say which fixture hits the face.

entries.title: Available Light
entries.text:
Available Light

Available light in available light cinematography is the illumination already at the location before the crew adds or changes units: sun, sky, or existing interior fixtures. You commit to the hour and the existing contrast.

Create this Available Light

Narrative function

The day is the gaffer. , a kitchen with one overhead, a station with sodium: you expose for what is there and block actors into it.

Documentary and certain features treat that limitation as the look. It is the wrong tool when you need night-for-night control, a cheek triangle that the sun will not hold, or matching a scene across three hours.

If you add a bounce board you have already left pure available and entered a small bounce or naturalistic cheat.

How it works

Do not add lights. Choose sun angle, weather, and existing fixtures.

Hardness is the sun's (hard when clear, soft when overcast). Color is the real Kelvin of that hour: high sun near 5600K, late sun warmer, interiors whatever the building installed.

Expose for faces or for sky, not both if the ratio is huge. Prompt: Available light only on [Subject], sun, sky, or existing interior fixtures, documentary humility, no added units.

When to use it

Use it when you will commit to the hour you have, a ridge, a real kitchen, a street at the time the story needs. Do not use it if you plan to sneak in an HMI and still call it available.

Compared with similar shots

Motivated lighting adds hidden units that imitate the world. Naturalistic ambient is crafted to look unstyled and may include lights.

Golden hour and blue hour are specific available conditions. Practical lighting can be available if the fixtures already exist and you do not enhance them.

Naturalistic AmbientInvisible craft.

Motivated LightingRealism with control. Light like a world, not a studio.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Days of Heaven waited on natural edges of the day. The Revenant committed to location sun, overcast, and fire already in the space.

The grammar is patience and geography, not a gel called natural.

Prompt it

Forbid added units. " Name the hour and the existing source.

Do not list movie lamps.

Use in Image Generator

Available light only on [Subject], sun, sky, or existing interior fixtures, documentary humility, no added units.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is motivated lighting sold as available. The tell is a perfect fill on the shadow cheek at noon in open sun.

Fix it by removing extra units, or by renaming the setup motivated.

Questions

What is available light in film?

Existing illumination at a location before the crew adds or changes anything: sun, sky, or fixtures already there.

Available light vs naturalistic ambient

Available light means no added units. Naturalistic ambient is a crafted wrap that looks like room or sky, and it may use hidden lights.

When should I use available light?

Use it when the real hour and place are the point, and you can schedule for them. Skip it when continuity or a specific portrait pattern must be locked.

How do I prompt available light for AI image or video?

State sun, sky, or existing fixtures only, no added units. Name the time of day and the real source direction.

entries.title: Naturalistic Ambient
entries.text:
Naturalistic Ambient

Naturalistic ambient lighting wraps the subject in soft, directionally plausible room or sky tone so the craft reads as unstyled even when units are added. Shadows stay believable; nothing announces a movie lamp.

Create this Naturalistic Ambient

Narrative function

Invisible craft. A kitchen, a car, a holiday apartment: the light feels like the space, and the audience stops thinking about lighting.

Independent drama uses it so emotion is not underlined by a slash of hard key. It is the wrong tool when the story wants a theatrical cut, a butterfly, or a concert edge.

If the wrap is so complete that direction dies, you have flattened the room. Naturalistic still has a window side.

How it works

Start from the real window or overhead, then add large soft sources or bounce along that same axis. Keep ratios gentle (often under 4:1).

Hardness is soft; color matches the space (daylight through glass, warm tungsten mix at dusk). Avoid hair lights that cannot be a ceiling and kickers that cannot be a lamp.

Prompt: Naturalistic ambient wrap on [Subject], soft room tone, believable shadow, window-motivated without theatricality.

When to use it

Use it for quiet contemporary drama, a memory that should not look lit. Do not use it for noir graphic or a glamour package.

Compared with similar shots

Available light forbids adding units; this look may add them. Soft light is the hardness you will use.

Motivated lighting is the justification; naturalistic ambient is the overall unstyled wrap. Bounce light is a common method.

High-key is brighter and more even than most lived-in rooms.

Soft LightBeauty, memory, or kindness.

Available LightCommit to the hour you have.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Aftersun lets holiday rooms and sky feel found. Manchester by the Sea keeps New England interiors and winter daylight in a believable wrap.

Neither film advertises a key position even when units are surely there.

Prompt it

Ask for room tone, not a named portrait pattern. " Name a window side.

Forbid hair lights and hard kickers.

Use in Image Generator

Naturalistic ambient wrap on [Subject], soft room tone, believable shadow, window-motivated without theatricality.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is three-point or frankly available noon sun. The tell is a rim that no ceiling could throw, or harsh unshaped sun while you asked for quiet.

Fix it by aligning every unit to the window and softening until direction remains only as a gentle side.

Questions

What is naturalistic ambient in film?

A crafted wrap that looks like ordinary room or sky light. Units may be added, but direction, hardness, and color stay plausible for the space.

Naturalistic ambient vs available light

Available light uses only what exists. Naturalistic ambient imitates that existence and may hide lights to keep faces readable.

When should I use naturalistic ambient?

Use it for quiet drama that should not look lit. Skip it when graphic shadow or glamour is the point.

How do I prompt naturalistic ambient for AI image or video?

Ask for a soft room-tone wrap, believable shadow, window-motivated, no theatrical hair light or hard kicker. Name the window side.
