entries.title: Bounce Light
entries.text:
Bounce Light

Bounce lighting reflects light from a surface (wall, ceiling, poly, card) before it reaches the subject, so the apparent source becomes that large surface. Direction remains, but shadow edges soften and wrap.

Create this Bounce Light

Narrative function

You keep a window side or a lamp side without the brutality of the bare source. Faces wrap, rooms feel inhabited, and the key still has a direction because the bounce surface occupies a place in the world.

Period interiors and daylight rooms use it so skin does not speckle. It is the wrong tool when you need razor shadows, a gobo pattern, or a hard split.

Bounce is a method, not a facial pattern: it is not Rembrandt, not split, not butterfly. Those patterns die if you bounce too much.

How it works

Aim a lamp or the sun at a white or neutral surface, then let that surface light the subject. Larger and closer bounce means softer light.

Color picks up the bounce surface: white stays honest, a cream wall warms, a green wall will tint. The key side is the side of the bounce, not the lamp behind it.

Prompt: Bounce light on [Subject], key ricocheted off a white wall or poly, wrapping, gentle, large-source softness.

When to use it

Use it to soften without losing direction, a face by a white wall, a ceiling bounce in a low room. Do not bounce when you need a crisp nose shadow or projected blinds.

Compared with similar shots

Soft light can also come from a large silk in line with the lamp; bounce specifically reflects first. Window light is often bounced by walls after entering.

Fill light is a job bounce often performs. Motivated lighting may use bounce to imitate a wall the story has.

Hard light is the quality bounce destroys.

Soft LightBeauty, memory, or kindness.

Window LightDay interiors without looking lit.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Cries and Whispers uses wrap from walls and rooms so faces glow without a hard edge. The Tree of Life often lets sun hit interiors and bounce into skin.

The method is the ricochet, not a filter named soft.

Prompt it

Name the reflecting surface. " State the wall's side and color.

Forbid a small bare bulb as the apparent source.

Use in Image Generator

Bounce light on [Subject], key ricocheted off a white wall or poly, wrapping, gentle, large-source softness.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a bare hard key or a frontal silk that is not a bounce. The tell is razor nose shadows, or a source that still looks small.

Fix it by making the last surface before the face a large wall or board, and by naming that surface.

Questions

What is bounce light in film?

Light that hits a surface and then the subject. The surface becomes a large, softer source while keeping some direction.

Bounce light vs soft light

Soft light is the quality (large apparent source). Bounce is one method of getting that quality, by reflecting off a wall, ceiling, or board.

When should I use bounce light?

Use it when you want wrap and gentle shadows without losing which side is keyed. Skip it for hard graphic shadow.

How do I prompt bounce light for AI image or video?

Say the key ricochets off a white wall or poly before hitting the subject. Name the bounce side and the wrap. No small bare source on the face.

entries.title: Hard Light
entries.text:
Hard Light

Hard light in hard light cinematography comes from a small apparent source and produces crisp shadow edges and specular definition on skin, metal, and walls. Texture is amplified; falloff can still be steep or long depending on distance.

Create this Hard Light

Narrative function

Noon sun, a bare bulb, an interrogation lamp: pores, sweat, and brick become graphic. Noir and westerns use it so a hat brim cuts a clean triangle on the face and a body throws a readable double on the wall.

It is the wrong tool for kindness, memory, or a beauty close-up that should wrap. Hard is not the same as bright, and not the same as low-key.

You can have a dim hard source in a black room, or a blazing hard sun in a high-key desert.

How it works

Use a small source relative to the subject: distant sun, bare tungsten, a focused Fresnel, a snooted LED. Distance makes it harder (smaller apparent size).

Color is often white daylight or tungsten; gels stay saturated because the source is specular. Pair with flags for gobo patterns.

Prompt: Hard light on [Subject] from a small distant source, razor shadow edges, texture amplified, noir graphic.

When to use it

Use it for grit, noon sun, or interrogation, a street at midday, a bulb over a table. Do not use it as default beauty on a romantic close-up.

Compared with similar shots

Soft light is the opposite quality: large source, gradual edges. Gobo lighting needs hard light to throw a sharp pattern.

Low-key lighting often uses hard sources but is a ratio. Split lighting often wants a hard 90-degree key.

Bounce is how you destroy hardness.

Soft LightBeauty, memory, or kindness.

Gobo LightingThe room writes on the person.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Big Combo and Se7en cut faces and rooms with small, hard sources. Once Upon a Time in the West lets hard sun define hats, dust, and wood.

The edge of the shadow is the grammar.

Prompt it

Name a small distant source and razor edges. Use: "Hard light on [Subject] from a small distant source, razor shadow edges, texture amplified, noir graphic." Forbid silks, wrap, and cloudy softness unless weather is the point.

Use in Image Generator

Hard light on [Subject] from a small distant source, razor shadow edges, texture amplified, noir graphic.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is soft light with high contrast. The tell is fuzzy shadow edges on the nose and table.

Fix it by shrinking the apparent source (remove diffusion, move it farther, or switch to sun and a clear sky).

Questions

What is hard light in film?

Light from a small apparent source that makes crisp shadows and specular texture. Noon sun and a bare bulb are typical.

Hard light vs soft light

Hard: small source, sharp shadow edge, more texture. Soft: large source, gradual shadow edge, more wrap.

When should I use hard light?

Use it for grit, noon, interrogation, or graphic noir. Skip it when the face should be treated kindly.

How do I prompt hard light for AI image or video?

Specify a small distant source, razor shadow edges, amplified texture. No silk, no wrap, no cloudy softness.

entries.title: Soft Light
entries.text:
Soft Light

Soft light in soft light cinematography comes from a large apparent source and produces gradual shadow transitions and wrap around the face or body. Speculars get larger and dimmer; texture is reduced.

Create this Soft Light

Narrative function

Kindness, memory, overcast, a north window: the key still has a side, but the nose shadow is a gradient. Skin holds, rooms feel breathable.

You can still have contrast if the fill is low; softness is not high-key. It is the wrong tool for a gobo of blinds, a noon duel, or a split that needs a knife edge.

If the source becomes so large it surrounds the subject, direction dies and you have ambient soup.

How it works

Make the last surface before the subject large: silk, book light, overcast sky, big window, bounce wall. Closer and larger is softer.

Color is often daylight 5600K through diffusion, or tungsten through a large shade. Keep a key side.

Prompt: Soft wrapping light on [Subject] from a large source, gentle shadow transitions, luminous skin, north-window daylight.

When to use it

Use it for beauty, memory, or kindness, a daylight interior, a close-up that should not cut pores into craters. Do not use it when you need projected pattern or interrogation.

Compared with similar shots

Hard light is the opposite quality. Bounce light is a method of getting soft.

Window light is often large and soft by architecture. Glam uses soft keys plus diffusion and catchlights.

High-key lighting uses soft sources and a lot of fill; you can have soft low-key if the wrap is large but isolated.

Bounce LightSoften without losing direction.

Window LightDay interiors without looking lit.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Tree of Life and Call Me by Your Name let large daylight sources wrap skin and rooms. The softness is the size of sky and window, not a beauty filter named glow.

Prompt it

Name a large source and gentle edges. " Keep a key side.

Forbid razor nose shadows.

Use in Image Generator

Soft wrapping light on [Subject] from a large source, gentle shadow transitions, luminous skin, Vermeer daylight.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is hard light or directionless ambient. The tell is razor edges, or no key side at all.

Fix it by enlarging the source and keeping it on one side of the face.

Questions

What is soft light in film?

Light from a large apparent source that wraps the subject and makes shadow edges gradual. Texture is reduced; direction can still exist.

Soft light vs bounce light

Soft describes the quality. Bounce is one way to create it, by reflecting off a large surface. A silk in line with the lamp is another way.

When should I use soft light?

Use it for kindness, memory, and most daylight interiors. Skip it when you need graphic shadow or a sharp gobo.

entries.title: Side Lighting
entries.text:
Side Lighting

Side lighting keys primarily from one side, around 90 degrees to the camera-subject line, so shape and texture are emphasized. Half the form goes toward light, half toward shadow.

Create this Side Lighting

Narrative function

A face or a landscape becomes sculpture. Sweat, wood grain, and cheekbones show because the light rakes.

Action and crime use it so bodies have planes; portraits use it when character should look carved. It is the wrong tool for a passport-readable hero or a beauty wrap.

Side lighting a room is not automatically split lighting. Split is the facial center-line cut with almost no wrap.

Side can still graze a shoulder, a horse, a wall.

How it works

Place the key at about 90 degrees, at a height that fits the story (eye height for a face, raking low sun for ground texture). Hardness is often hard so texture reads; soft side light exists as a large window in a side wall.

Color follows that source. Control wrap with flags if you need a truer split.

Prompt: Pure side light at 90 degrees on [Subject], half the face brilliant, half gone, texture and duality.

When to use it

Use it to carve a face or a body like sculpture, a raking desert, a sweat-lit fight. Do not use it as default coverage on a two-shot that needs both people open.

Compared with similar shots

Split lighting is the hard facial version of this direction. Cross lighting uses two opposing side keys.

Kicker is a side-back accent, not a key. Short lighting and broad lighting depend on head turn relative to camera, not on 90 degrees as such.

Split LightingDuality made literal.

Cross LightingStage, sweat, or two moral sources.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Apocalypse Now rakes faces with hard side sources in the dark. Sicario uses raking sun and side keys so landscape and faces have grain.

The job is the 90-degree rake, not a mood.

Prompt it

Put the lamp at 90 degrees. " Name hardness.

Say whether the body or only the face is raked.

Use in Image Generator

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Rembrandt (too frontal) or cross lighting (a second key). The tell is a cheek triangle, or rims on both sides.

Fix it by parking one key at 90 and killing the opposite unit.

Questions

What is side lighting in film?

Light from about 90 degrees that emphasizes shape and texture. One side of the subject is bright; the other falls away.

Side lighting vs split lighting

Side lighting is the direction, usable on faces, bodies, and rooms. Split lighting is a facial pattern with a hard vertical cut and almost no wrap.

When should I use side lighting?

Use it to carve texture and duality. Skip it when both eyes must be openly keyed for a public conversation.

How do I prompt side lighting for AI image or video?

Place a single key at 90 degrees. State half the form brilliant, half gone, and name hard or soft. No second key on the far side.

entries.title: Top Light
entries.text:
Top Light

Top lighting is illumination from directly above the subject, falling on forehead, nose bridge, and shoulders while the eye sockets and the underside of the chin go into shadow. The source is a ceiling, a rig, or a high practical, not a frontal beauty key.

Create this Top Light

Narrative function

Power sitting in a chair, or guilt: the head is a skull with a lid of light. Crime bosses, interrogations, and some night exteriors use overhead so the eyes recede.

The person is still human; the pupils must not emit. It is the wrong tool for glamour.

If you bring the source forward of the head you get butterfly. If you need a catchlight, add a tiny eye light rather than lowering the overhead until it becomes a frontal key.

How it works

Hang a lamp or use a ceiling practical directly above, flagged so it does not rake the nose as a frontal. Hardness can be hard (bare bulb) for a skull, or a bit softer (shaded pendant) for a diner.

Color is often tungsten, sometimes cool industrial. Keep exposure on the forehead, not in the sockets, unless you add a separate eye glint.

Prompt: A lamp directly above [Subject], light falling on forehead and shoulders, eye sockets in shadow, human eyes, no light emitting from the pupils.

When to use it

Use it for a figure of power in a chair, a diner pendant, a guilty face under a garage bulb. Do not use it as beauty lighting.

Compared with similar shots

Underlighting is the opposite direction, from below. Butterfly lighting is high but still in front of the face.

Low-key lighting is the ratio that often houses top light. Hair light is behind and above, not a downward key on the forehead.

Cameo may use a top pool but is about isolating the figure in void.

Low-Key LightingMystery, crime, or moral night.

UnderlightingThe source is fire, a screen on the floor, or a monster.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Godfather is the famous overhead office: forehead and hands, eyes in wells. The Batman (2022) uses overhead rain and practicals so faces sit under lids of light.

The sockets stay dark on purpose.

Prompt it

Put the lamp on the ceiling axis. Use: "A lamp directly above [Subject], light falling on forehead and shoulders, eye sockets in shadow, human eyes, no light emitting from the pupils." Forbid frontal beauty fill.

Use in Image Generator

A lamp directly above [Subject], light falling on forehead and shoulders, eye sockets in shadow, human eyes, no light emitting from the pupils.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is butterfly or glowing eyes. The tell is an under-nose butterfly with open sockets, or pupils that shine like LEDs.

Fix it by moving the source truly overhead and keeping eyes as dark human surfaces with at most a tiny catch.

Questions

What is top light in film?

Light from directly above that hits forehead and shoulders and drops the eye sockets into shadow. It is a downward key, not a hair rim.

Top light vs butterfly lighting

Butterfly is high and in front, opening both eyes with a small nose shadow. Top light is overhead enough that the sockets hollow.

When should I use top light?

Use it for power, guilt, a pendant over a table, a boss in a chair. Skip it for glamour.

Place a lamp directly above. Light on forehead and shoulders, eye sockets in shadow, human eyes, no light from the pupils.

entries.title: Underlighting
entries.text:
Underlighting

uplighting

Underlighting, also called uplighting, lights from below the face so shadows climb the cheekbones and the tops of the eye sockets. The modeling is the reverse of daylight and often reads as uncanny.

Create this Underlighting

Narrative function

The source is fire, a screen on the floor, a flashlight under a chin, or a monster. Faces invert: the brow ridge goes dark, the nostrils and chin light up.

Horror and campfire talk use the same physics; only the object changes. It is the wrong tool for ordinary conversation under a ceiling.

A candle on a table can underlight if it sits below the chin, but candlelight is a source type that can also sit beside a face. Underlighting is the direction.

How it works

Place a lamp, flame, or panel below the chin, pointing up. Keep it close so inverse-square falloff hits the face and dies on the ceiling.

Hardness is often hard or small-soft (a phone screen is a smallish source). Color is flame-warm, screen-cool, or theatrical green; the climb of the shadows is the tell.

Prompt: A lamp on the table below [Subject]'s chin, pointing up. Shadows climb the cheekbones and eye sockets.

The source is under the face, not beside it.

When to use it

Use it when the source is fire, a floor screen, or a threat under the chin. Do not use it as a default beauty fill from a white card unless you want unease.

Compared with similar shots

Top light is the opposite. Candlelight may underlight if the flame is low, but a candelabra at face height is more of a small frontal or side key.

Practical lighting is the visible object; underlighting is where it sits. Glam sometimes uses a weak under fill (a reflector) that must stay far below key so it does not invert the face.

Top LightPower sitting in a chair, or guilt.

CandlelightPeriod night or ritual.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

James Whale's Frankenstein (1931) underlights the creature so the brow and sockets invert. Hereditary uses low sources and ritual light to the same uncanny effect.

The shadows must climb, not slide sideways.

Prompt it

Put the source under the chin. Use: "A lamp on the table below [Subject]'s chin, pointing up.

Shadows climb the cheekbones and eye sockets. " Name fire, screen, or bulb.

Use in Image Generator

A lamp on the table below [Subject]'s chin, pointing up. Shadows climb the cheekbones and eye sockets. The source is under the face, not beside it.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is side lighting or a candle off to the side. The tell is a left-right split instead of shadows that climb.

Fix it by lowering the source below the jaw and aiming up.

Questions

What is underlighting in film?

Lighting from below the face so shadows climb the cheeks and sockets. It inverts ordinary daylight modeling and often feels uncanny.

Underlighting vs top light

Top light comes from above and hollows the eyes from overhead. Underlighting comes from below and lights the chin and nostrils while the brow goes dark.

When should I use underlighting?

Use it for firelight below the face, a screen on the floor, or a horror invert. Skip it for ordinary daylight talk.

How do I prompt underlighting for AI image or video?

Place the lamp or flame under the chin, pointing up. State that shadows climb the cheekbones and sockets, source under the face, not beside it.

entries.title: Cross Lighting
entries.text:
Cross Lighting

Cross lighting keys subjects from opposite side directions, so each person or each side of a body gets a key and a far rim. It is common in dialogue coverage, stage, and concert work.

Create this Cross Lighting

Narrative function

Two moral sources, or just two people who both need a face. Sweat on a drummer, a duet, a fight: edges appear on both sides because each lamp is someone else's key.

Theatrical energy comes from the dual rims, not from smoke alone. It is the wrong tool for a single-source room, a motivated night interior with one lamp, or a true split on one face.

If both keys are equally frontal you have flattened the pair. If only one side is keyed, you are back to side lighting.

How it works

Place two keys roughly opposite, each about 70 to 110 degrees off the camera-subject axis, often slightly back so they rim as well as key. Hardness is often hard for concerts, softer for dialogue.

Color may match, or each side can carry a different gel (warm versus cool) as two worlds. Flag them off the lens.

Prompt: Cross lighting on [Subject] from two opposing keys, dual rims, theatrical or concert edges on both sides.

When to use it

Use it for stage, sweat, or two people who each need a key from the other's side. Do not use it in a one-lamp apartment unless you want that apartment to feel like a concert.

Compared with similar shots

Side lighting is one direction. Rim light is a thin rear edge, not a second key.

Kicker is a single far-side accent. Three-point lighting uses key, fill, and back, not two opposing keys.

Split is one face cut by one key.

Rim LightGraphic silhouette with just enough flesh.

Side LightingCarve a face like sculpture.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Whiplash cross-lights the band so rims and sweat read from both sides. Concert films and stage sequences in A Star Is Born use opposing keys as the grammar of performance.

Two sources, two edges.

Prompt it

Name two opposing keys. " Specify colors if they differ.

Forbid a single-side split.

Use in Image Generator

Cross lighting on [Subject] from two opposing keys, dual rims, theatrical or concert energy, edges on both sides.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is one side key or a frontal pair of fills. The tell is one rim only, or two flat cheeks.

Fix it by parking hard or medium keys opposite each other, slightly back, and letting each throw a far edge.

Questions

What is cross lighting in film?

Lighting from opposite sides so a subject or a pair gets keys (and often rims) from both directions. Common in dialogue, stage, and concerts.

Cross lighting vs side lighting

Side lighting is one 90-degree key. Cross lighting is two opposing keys, so both sides of the body or both people have an edge.

When should I use cross lighting?

Use it for stage, concerts, or two-handed coverage that must key both faces. Skip it for a single motivated lamp.

How do I prompt cross lighting for AI image or video?

Specify two opposing keys and dual rims. Name hardness and any color split. Not a single-side face cut.

entries.title: Window Light
entries.text:
Window Light

Window light in window light cinematography is illumination shaped to appear as light entering through a window: a large, directional source with falloff into the room. The architecture is the modifier.

Create this Window Light

Narrative function

Day interiors without looking lit. A figure sits in the falloff, one side toward glass, the far wall dying.

Painterly rooms, period houses, and quiet dramas use the window as the only key so the hour is readable. It is the wrong tool at night (unless moonlight through glass is the story), or when you need a hard bulb.

A window is not automatically bounce; bounce happens after the light hits a wall. A window can be hard if the sun is direct and small in the frame of the glass.

How it works

Use real sky or a large source outside the glass, plus sheers if you want wrap. Direction is the window's side.

Hardness: overcast or north light is soft; direct sun through dirty glass is harder and may throw a patch. Color is daylight, cooler if north sky, warmer late.

Let inverse-square and flags create falloff toward the room. Prompt: Window light as the only key on [Subject], large soft directional source, falloff into the room, painterly interior.

When to use it

Use it for a day interior that should not look studio-lit, a sitting room, a workshop. Do not use a frontal silk that ignores the window's actual wall.

Compared with similar shots

Soft light is the usual quality of north windows. Motivated lighting is the logic that lets you hide a source outside that window.

Bounce is the wall ricochet after entry. Available light uses the real window without adding.

Golden hour through a window is a specific color and angle of this source.

Soft LightBeauty, memory, or kindness.

Motivated LightingRealism with control. Light like a world, not a studio.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Girl with a Pearl Earring (2003) builds interiors as if Vermeer's window were the key. The Danish Girl uses large directional day interiors with falloff.

The grammar is glass, falloff, and one side, not a painting to clone.

Prompt it

Make the window the only key. Use: "Window light as the only key on [Subject], large soft directional source, falloff into the room, painterly interior." Name which wall holds the glass and whether the sky is overcast or late sun.

Use in Image Generator

Window light as the only key on [Subject], large soft directional source, falloff into the room, painterly interior.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a frontal soft key that does not match the window wall, or a hard gobo of blinds when you asked for wrap. The tell is a key from a blank wall.

Fix it by putting the bright side on the glass and letting the room fall off.

Questions

What is window light in film?

Light shaped as if it enters through a window: large, directional, with falloff into the room. The window is the source and the modifier.

Window light vs bounce light

Window light is the entry from glass and sky. Bounce is a ricochet off a surface, which a window may cause once it hits a wall, but bounce is not the window itself.

When should I use window light?

Use it for day interiors that should feel architectural rather than studio-lit. Skip it when the story is a night bulb.

How do I prompt window light for AI image or video?

State window light as the only key, large directional source, falloff into the room. Name the window wall and the sky condition.

entries.title: Candlelight
entries.text:
Candlelight

Low-light period interior

Candlelight in candlelight cinematography is a small warm practical or a simulated flame with rapid falloff, often around 1800K, that carves faces near the flame and lets the rest of the room die. Flicker is part of the source, not a grade.

Volume

Create this Candlelight

Narrative function

Period night and ritual live on this physics: people lean in because the light does not travel. A card table, a vigil, a cabin: faces emerge from the room instead of being separately lit for the viewer.

Darkness stays as lived space. It is the wrong tool for a wide court that must stay evenly readable, or for a modern kitchen.

Not every period film used only candles; Barry Lyndon's approach is specifically documented, often with fast lenses and sometimes hidden augmentation matched to the flame.

How it works

Cluster real or LED candles close to faces. The apparent source is small, so shadows are fairly hard, but multiple flames wrap a little.

Falloff is steep (inverse square from a tiny source). Color is deep warm, well below tungsten.

If the cluster sits below the chin you will also get some underlighting; if it sits at eye height it is a small frontal or three-quarter key. Prompt: Candlelight on [Subject], warm 1800K flicker, faces carved by flame, deep falloff.

When to use it

Use it for period night or ritual, a table of cards, a prayer. Do not claim a huge hall is only candles if you have even, modern fill.

Compared with similar shots

Practical lighting is the broader class; candle is the small flame subset. Underlighting is direction, which a low candle can cause.

Motivated lighting may hide units that match 1800K along the same throw. Chiaroscuro is the contrast language this falloff often creates.

Glam will fight the falloff.

Practical LightingLet the set light the face.

UnderlightingThe source is fire, a screen on the floor, or a monster.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Barry Lyndon is the documented candlelit card-table and evening interior, with fast optics and credible falloff. The Witch keeps flame as the logic of night in a dark New England.

Faces fade with distance from the cluster.

Barry Lyndon 1975Candlelit card-table and evening interiors.

Prompt it

Keep the flame small and close. " Cluster the candles, kill electric fill, and let corners go dark.

No orange wash on a bright room.

Use in Video Generator

An eighteenth-century card game lit as if only by clustered candles on the table. Faces fade quickly into darkness with distance from the flames, warm uneven illumination, believable flame detail and subdued room corners. A slow restrained gesture, no bright modern fill or electric orange wash.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a tungsten wash or underlighting from a big movie lamp. The tell is even exposure ten feet from the candle, or a single huge orange gel.

Fix it by making falloff rapid and keeping color at flame Kelvin.

Questions

What is candlelight in film?

A small warm flame source with rapid falloff and flicker. Faces near the flame are modeled; the rest of the room can go dark.

Candlelight vs underlighting

Candlelight is the source type. Underlighting is a direction from below. A candle under the chin underlights; a candle at eye height keys from the front or side.

When should I use candlelight?

Use it for period night, vigils, and tables where people must lean toward the flame. Skip it for even modern interiors.

Specify warm 1800K flicker, faces carved by flame, deep falloff. Cluster candles close. No bright modern fill.

entries.title: Neon Practicals
entries.text:
Neon Practicals

Neon practicals are visible neon or similar sign tubes used as actual keys or strong accents, coloring the subject with magenta, cyan, or other tube hues instead of a hidden white source. The city fixture is the lamp.

Create this Neon Practicals

Narrative function

Night streets, hotels, and rain: the sign is not decoration. Wet pavement bounces the same hue back up.

Mixed gels are honest because different signs disagree. Faces pick up the nearest tube as a key and the next one as a kicker.

It is the wrong tool for a daylight office, or for a teal-and-orange grade with no tubes in frame. If the neon is only in the background and a white key lights the face, you have set dressing, not neon practicals.

How it works

Put working tubes in frame close enough to expose. Hardness is that of a long, thin source: relatively soft along the tube, harder across it, with specular lines in eyes and on wet cloth.

Color is the gas and the gel: magenta, cyan, red, green, often mixed. Wet-down helps bounce.

Prompt: Neon practicals coloring [Subject], magenta and cyan signs as real keys, wet bounce, mixed gels, night-city chromatics.

When to use it

Use it when the city is the lighting department, a wet street, a motel sign, a night market. Do not use a white key and a neon wallpaper.

Compared with similar shots

Practical lighting is the parent class. Motivated lighting can hide units that match a sign's hue.

Blue hour often mixes with neon as warm and cool together. Cool blue and warm amber are grades; neon is a physical tube.

Cross lighting happens when two signs oppose.

Practical LightingLet the set light the face.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

Key LightDecide where the world is lit from. Everything else follows.

In film

Blade Runner uses signage and tubes as interior and street keys. Chungking Express lets Hong Kong neon hit faces at mixed hues.

Drive keeps magenta and cyan signs as real contributors on wet night streets.

Prompt it

Make the signs the keys. " Name which tube hits which cheek.

Forbid a white beauty key.

Use in Image Generator

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a white key plus neon bokeh. The tell is neutral skin in front of colored circles.

Fix it by letting the nearest tube be the key and allowing mixed color on the face.

Questions

What is neon practical lighting in film?

Visible neon or similar signs used as real lights on the subject. The tube's color becomes the key or a strong accent, often with wet bounce.

Neon practicals vs practical lighting

Practical lighting includes any visible fixture. Neon practicals are the subset where gas tubes or similar signs supply the hue and the exposure.

When should I use neon practicals?

Use them for night-city faces that should be colored by signs. Skip them if the neon is only background decoration.

How do I prompt neon practicals for AI image or video?

State magenta and cyan signs as real keys, wet bounce, mixed gels. The face takes the tube color. No hidden white movie key.

entries.title: Golden Hour
entries.text:
Golden Hour

Twilight photographyGolden-hour window

Golden hour in golden hour cinematography is low-angle warm sunlight shortly after sunrise or before sunset, when the sun is near the horizon. Shadows go long; the light is directional, warm, and brief.

Create this Golden Hour

Narrative function

You have a short window in which ordinary action looks transient because the sun is leaving or arriving. Faces rake, dust shows, and the sky still has brightness.

Farms, roads, and childhood exteriors wait on this hour because it will not hold. It is the wrong tool if you need three hours of matching coverage, or if you mean the cool time after the sun is down.

An orange grade on midday sun is not golden hour. Direct late sun is still a hard-ish source; post-sunset wrap is blue hour or dusk ambient.

How it works

Point the scene at the low sun. Backlight is common (warm rim, long ground shadows toward camera); front or side rake also works.

Hardness is softer than noon because of atmosphere, but shadows remain defined. Color is warm amber, well below midday 5600K.

Rehearse before the window. Prompt: Golden hour backlight on [Subject], warm amber raking sun, long shadows, horizontal flare.

When to use it

Use it when the day is ending or beginning and the sun is still up, a last walk, a field, a ridge. Do not use an orange LUT on noon and call it this hour.

Compared with similar shots

Blue hour is after sunset or before sunrise, cool ambient, no hard sun disk lighting the subject. Available light is the method; golden hour is a specific available condition.

Backlight is a common placement of this sun. Warm amber is a grade that can fake the hue without the long shadows.

Blue HourDay is gone but the sky still works.

Available LightCommit to the hour you have.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Days of Heaven waited on farm and prairie edges of the day. The Tree of Life uses low-sun childhood passages.

The Revenant and Call Me by Your Name both treat late or early sun as a scheduled source, not a preset.

Days of Heaven 1978Farm and prairie scenes in the low-light edges of the day.

The Tree of Life 2011Natural-light childhood passages, including low-sun imagery.

Prompt it

Keep the sun low and real. " Say the sun is just above the horizon.

Forbid midday height and a full blue sky with no rake.

Use in Video Generator

Two farm workers walk beside a wheat field just after sunset. Soft luminous sky, low contrast on their faces, warm remnants on the horizon, no direct overhead sun. Gentle wind and patient lateral movement, natural exposure, no exaggerated orange filter.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is blue hour or an orange midday grade. The tell is a high sun, or a cool sky with no long shadows.

Fix it by lowering the sun, warming the key, and throwing long shadows.

Questions

What is golden hour in film?

Low-angle warm sunlight shortly after sunrise or before sunset. Shadows are long, color is warm, and the window is short.

Golden hour vs blue hour

Golden hour still has the sun above the horizon as a warm directional key. Blue hour is twilight with the sun down, a cool sky, and no hard sunlight.

When should I use golden hour?

Use it for a brief late or early exterior that can accept long shadows and changing light. Skip it if you cannot schedule the window.

How do I prompt golden hour for AI image or video?

entries.title: Blue Hour
entries.text:
Blue Hour

Blue hour in blue hour cinematography is cool ambient twilight before sunrise or after sunset, when the sun is below the horizon but the sky still glows. There is no hard sunlight; the sky is a large cool source, and warm practicals often kick in.

Create this Blue Hour

Narrative function

Day is gone but the sky still works as a wrap. Cities mix cobalt air with sodium, tungsten, and neon.

Crime and melancholy exteriors use this mix because faces can be cool while windows go warm. It is the wrong tool if you still want a sun disk raking the ground.

That is golden hour or late sun. A blue grade on night black is not blue hour.

You need residual sky luminance.

How it works

Expose for the glowing sky as a large, soft, overhead-to-side source, Kelvin high and cool. Add warm practicals (streetlights, windows, signs) as small hard or semi-hard accents.

Hardness of the wrap is soft; hardness of the lamps is whatever they are. Color contrast is the point: cool ambient versus warm fixtures.

Prompt: Blue hour wrap on [Subject], deep cobalt sky still glowing, warm practicals kicking in.

When to use it

Use it when the sun is down but the sky still holds, a city street, a platform, a rooftop. Do not use it for a hard sunset backlight.

Compared with similar shots

Golden hour still has directional warm sun. Neon practicals often appear inside blue hour as the warm or magenta notes.

Available light at this time is exactly this mix if you add nothing. Cool blue is a grade; blue hour is a real sky condition.

Motivated lighting can fake it with large cool overheads plus warm lamps.

Golden HourYou have twenty minutes of truth.

Neon PracticalsThe city is the lighting department.

In film

Heat and Collateral are built on Los Angeles twilight, digital-friendly cobalt air with sodium and tungsten. Drive uses the same urban mix of residual sky and signs.

The sky has to still be there.

Keep the sky luminous and cool. Use: "Blue hour wrap on [Subject], deep cobalt sky still glowing, warm practicals kicking in." Forbid a visible sun disk and a black night sky with no residual light.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is golden hour or night-for-night black. The tell is long warm sun shadows, or a sky with no glow.

Fix it by killing the sun, cooling the wrap, and turning practicals on against a still-bright sky.

Questions

What is blue hour in film?

Cool twilight before sunrise or after sunset, with the sun down and the sky still glowing. Warm practicals often contrast with that cool wrap.

Blue hour vs golden hour

Blue hour has no hard sun and a cool sky. Golden hour has the sun just above the horizon as a warm directional source with long shadows.

When should I use blue hour?

Use it for urban or exterior twilight when the sky still works and lamps are coming on. Skip it if you need raking sun.

entries.title: Dappled Light
entries.text:
Dappled Light

Dappled light is broken patches of brightness and shadow caused by foliage, water, blinds, or another irregular obstruction in a hard beam. The pattern is organic and often moving.

Create this Dappled Light

Narrative function

A tree writes on a coat. Jungle, orchard, and bedroom blinds turn a person into a field of spots.

Nature or architecture becomes the gobo without looking designed as a logo. It is the wrong tool for a clean beauty close-up or a graphic prison-bar statement.

If the pattern is a crisp logo or perfectly parallel slats, you have shifted toward gobo lighting. Dappled wants irregular leaf-shaped or caustic patches.

How it works

You need a relatively hard sun or lamp, plus an obstructing layer (leaves, a tree, water surface, dirty glass) between source and subject. Distance from gobo to subject controls softness of the patches.

Color is usually daylight. Wind or water makes the patches crawl.

Prompt: Sun through leaves on [Subject], irregular patches of brightness and leaf-shaped shadows on coat and horse, a real tree overhead.

When to use it

Use it when nature or blinds should break the key, a forest walk, a siesta under a tree. Do not use a clean unobstructed key and then paint spots in post as stickers.

Compared with similar shots

Gobo lighting is the designed version: a cucoloris, bars, or blinds placed to write a graphic. Dappled is irregular and usually natural.

Hard light is required for sharp patches. Window light through trees outside can be dappled.

Volumetric light shows beams in air; dappled shows patches on surfaces.

Gobo LightingThe room writes on the person.

Hard LightGrit, noon sun, or interrogation.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Thin Red Line lets jungle canopy break sun on soldiers. Moonlight uses broken daylight and night sources so bodies carry irregular patches.

The obstruction is real, not a texture overlay.

Prompt it

Name the obstruction. Use: "Sun through leaves on [Subject], irregular patches of brightness and leaf-shaped shadows on coat and horse, a real tree overhead." Forbid a clean unpatterned key and a venetian-bar prison graphic unless blinds are the story.

Use in Image Generator

Sun through leaves on [Subject], irregular patches of brightness and leaf-shaped shadows on coat and horse, a real tree overhead.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a clean key or a designed gobo of bars. The tell is even skin, or perfectly parallel slats.

Fix it by putting a real tree, water, or irregular foliage in a hard beam.

Questions

What is dappled light in film?

Broken patches of light and shadow from foliage, water, or similar irregular obstruction in a hard beam. The pattern is organic.

Dappled light vs gobo lighting

Dappled is irregular, usually from nature. Gobo lighting places a designed pattern (cucoloris, blinds, bars) in the beam to throw a graphic.

When should I use dappled light?

Use it under trees, by water, or through messy glass when the world should break the key. Skip it for clean glamour or a prison-bar statement.

How do I prompt dappled light for AI image or video?

Put a real tree or irregular obstruction in hard sun. Ask for leaf-shaped or caustic patches on cloth and skin, not a clean key and not parallel bars.

entries.title: Gobo Lighting
entries.text:
Gobo Lighting

cucoloris

Gobo lighting places a pattern or object in a light beam (a gobo or cucoloris) so the source throws graphic shadows across face, body, and wall. The room writes on the person.

Create this Gobo Lighting

Narrative function

Venetian blinds, bars, branches cut as a design, a fan, a grille: the character wears the architecture. Noir and political interiors use it so a man is already in a cage before anyone speaks.

It is the wrong tool for invisible naturalism, or for random leaf scatter you do not want to look designed. If the pattern is irregular canopy, prefer dappled light.

Gobos need a hard enough source to stay readable.

How it works

Put a hard, small source through slats, a cut cucoloris, or a metal gobo in a fixture. Distance from pattern to subject sets how sharp the shadows are.

Key side is wherever that lamp sits, often high and off axis. Color is often white moonlight gel or hard tungsten.

Flag spill so the pattern is not washed out. Prompt: Gobo-patterned light on [Subject], venetian blinds, bars, or branches throwing graphic shadows across face and wall.

When to use it

Use it when the room should write on the person, blinds on a liar, bars on a prisoner. Do not use it as default texture on every close-up.

Compared with similar shots

Dappled light is irregular and natural. Hard light is the quality a gobo needs.

Window light through blinds is a motivated gobo. Split lighting is a half-face cut without a pattern.

Film noir is a genre look that often employs this tool.

Hard LightGrit, noon sun, or interrogation.

Dappled LightNature or blinds as gobo.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Conformist (Storaro) throws architectural slats and graphic shadows across faces and walls. Classic film noir uses blinds and bars as cages.

The pattern is placed, not accidental leaf scatter.

Prompt it

Name the object in the beam. " Specify a hard source.

Keep the pattern sharp enough to read.

Use in Image Generator

Gobo-patterned light on [Subject], venetian blinds, bars, or branches throwing graphic shadows across face and wall.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is dappled leaf scatter or soft wrap that eats the slats. The tell is fuzzy blobs, or no pattern at all.

Fix it by hardening the source and putting a real slat or cucoloris in the beam.

Questions

What is gobo lighting in film?

A pattern or object placed in a light beam so graphic shadows fall on the subject and the set. Venetian blinds and bars are common.

Gobo lighting vs dappled light

A gobo is a designed obstruction (cucoloris, blinds, bars). Dappled light is irregular, usually from foliage or water.

When should I use gobo lighting?

Use it when architecture should brand the face: blinds, bars, grilles. Skip it for unstyled naturalism.

How do I prompt gobo lighting for AI image or video?

Name blinds, bars, or a cucoloris in a hard beam, graphic shadows on face and wall. Keep the source hard enough for a sharp pattern.

entries.title: Volumetric Light
entries.text:
Volumetric Light

god rayscrepuscular rays

Volumetric lighting makes beams visible through haze, fog, dust, smoke, or other particles, so the air photographs as well as the subject. Also called god rays or crepuscular rays when the shafts are distinct.

Create this Volumetric Light

Narrative function

Air has to be photographed. A cathedral, a forest, a smoky archive: the beam is architecture.

The source implies a world outside the frame. Without particles you only see where the light lands, not the path it took.

It is the wrong tool in clean air if you still want shafts, or when haze is so thick that every depth plane flattens. Disconnected glowing stripes with no lamp are not volumetric light.

They are stickers.

How it works

You need a directional source (often hard, slightly back or high) and a scattering medium: haze, dust, rain, smoke. The camera usually sees some of the beam angle, which is why backlight helps.

Color follows the source: warm sun, cool window, searchlight white. Limit haze so foreground and background still separate.

Prompt: Volumetric rays through haze around [Subject], visible beams, dust in the shaft, cathedral or forest light as architecture.

When to use it

Use it when the air is part of the picture, a smoky interior, a forest morning, a searchlight. Do not add floating stripes with no source and no medium.

Compared with similar shots

Backlight is the direction that often reveals volume. Atmospheric haze is the medium.

Dappled light patterns surfaces; volume patterns the air. Epiphany may use a sudden shaft, but epiphany is a change timed to understanding.

Silhouette can sit inside a bright shaft if the figure stays dark.

Atmospheric HazeShow kilometers, not just meters.

BacklightSeparate a dark figure from a dark world.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Blade Runner 2049 builds interiors where dust and haze make shafts physical. The Tree of Life lets forest and interior sun become visible architecture.

Blade Runner (1982) searchlights through smoke are the same physics.

Prompt it

Name source plus medium. " Attach every beam to a window, sun, or searchlight.

Forbid disconnected glowing stripes.

Use in Image Generator

Volumetric god rays through haze around [Subject], visible beams, dust in the shaft, cathedral or forest light as architecture.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a backlight rim with no air, or painted god-ray stickers. The tell is stripes that ignore the lamp and the body.

Fix it by adding a scattering medium and a real rear or high source, then letting the body interrupt the beam.

Questions

What is volumetric light in film?

Beams made visible by haze, fog, dust, smoke, or particles. You photograph the path of the light, not only where it lands.

Volumetric light vs backlight

Backlight is the direction from behind. Volumetric light is the beam made visible in a medium. Backlight often helps you see that beam.

When should I use volumetric light?

Use it when air, dust, or smoke should be visible architecture. Skip it in clean air, or when haze would flatten every plane.

How do I prompt volumetric light for AI image or video?

Specify a real source and a scattering medium, visible beams, dust in the shaft. The body can interrupt the beam. No orphan glowing stripes.

entries.title: Cameo Lighting
entries.text:
Cameo Lighting

Cameo lighting isolates a lit subject against a predominantly dark environment, so the figure sits in a pool and the world falls to black. The person remains modeled; the set is withheld.

Create this Cameo Lighting

Narrative function

Erase the world, keep the person. Theatre-to-screen work, interrogation, and some comic-book night use a pool that does not describe architecture.

The audience gets a bust or a full figure as if cut from a void. It is the wrong tool when geography is the plot, or when you still want rain, furniture, and city in the frame.

If the figure is also unmodeled and the ground is bright, you have a silhouette, the inverse. If a hard circle with a visible edge is the point, prefer spotlight.

How it works

Key the subject (any portrait pattern) and kill all ambient and bounce with black wrap, distance, and flags. The background goes underexposed to black, not to a dimly readable room (low-key can still imply walls).

Hardness and color are free; isolation is the job. Prompt: Cameo lighting on [Subject], figure isolated in a pool against a black void, theatrical isolation, no environment.

When to use it

Use it when the world should vanish and the person remain, a confession, a stage aside. Do not use it for a chase that needs corridors.

Compared with similar shots

Spotlight is a hard-edged theatrical pool from a focused instrument. Cameo is the isolation result, which can use a softer key.

Low-key lighting still allows a dark room to exist. High-key lighting is the opposite field.

Epiphany is a change of light timed to thought, not a static void. Silhouette puts a dark figure on a bright field.

Low-Key LightingMystery, crime, or moral night.

High-Key LightingComedy, heaven, hospital, or candy.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Batman isolates figures in pools against withheld environments. Stage-to-screen work, including dark-stage passages in Birdman, treats the actor as a cutout in black.

The Elephant Man also parks bodies in isolated pools. The set is missing on purpose.

Prompt it

Kill the room. " Keep the face modeled.

Forbid a readable set and a bright sky.

Use in Image Generator

Cameo lighting on [Subject], figure isolated in a pool against a black void, theatrical spotlight, no environment.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is low-key with a still-visible room, or silhouette. The tell is furniture in the dark, or an unlit figure on a bright ground.

Fix it by exposing the person and letting the background go truly black.

Questions

What is cameo lighting in film?

A lit, modeled subject isolated against a predominantly dark or black environment. The world is withheld; the figure remains.

Cameo lighting vs spotlight

Cameo is the isolation: figure on void. A spotlight is a focused hard pool with a visible circle, one way of making a cameo, not the only way.

When should I use cameo lighting?

Use it when the person is the only geography that matters. Skip it when the room, street, or weather must remain.

How do I prompt cameo lighting for AI image or video?

Isolate the figure in a pool against a black void, no environment, face still modeled. Not a silhouette and not a dim but readable room.

entries.title: Epiphany
entries.text:
Epiphany

Epiphany lighting is a change of illumination that makes a face or figure suddenly the brightest readable fact in the room as a realization lands. The light finds the person; it is timed to understanding, not left as a static setup.

Volume

Create this Epiphany

Narrative function

Thought becomes visible. A dim interior, a forest, a chapel: something shifts (a cloud, a door, a hidden unit, a match) and the face takes the key as if the idea switched a lamp.

Spiritual and interior films use the change; the audience reads insight as exposure. It is the wrong tool for a whole scene that is merely pretty, or for a jump scare flash.

If the pool never changes, you have cameo or a static shaft. If the beam is only atmosphere, you have volumetric light without a thought.

How it works

Start under, then raise a motivated source on the face: sun through cloud, a door opening, a practical turned up, a flagged unit revealed. Direction often comes from above or behind so it can feel given rather than a frontal beauty key.

Hardness can be soft wrap or a sudden shaft; color often goes warmer or clearer than the preceding gloom. In video, the change is the shot.

Prompt: Epiphany light on [Subject], a sudden intelligible brightness, as if the thought itself switched a lamp. Motion: Light finds [Subject] as a realization lands, the face becoming the brightest fact in the room.

When to use it

Use it when understanding should be visible, a decision, a grace, a confession that lands. Do not use a random brightness bump with no story cause.

Compared with similar shots

Cameo lighting isolates a figure in a static pool. Volumetric light shows beams in air; epiphany may use that, but the job is the timed change on a face.

Spotlight is a theatrical instrument, not necessarily a thought. High-key is a whole-frame ratio, not a reveal.

Cameo LightingErase the world. Keep the person.

Volumetric LightAir has to be photographed, not just the subject.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

The Tree of Life lets sun and interior light arrive as if attention itself brightened. Silence uses sudden or given light on faces at moments of spiritual crisis.

The grammar is the change, not a lens flare sticker.

Prompt it

Write the before and after. Still: "Epiphany light on [Subject], a sudden intelligible brightness, as if the thought itself switched a lamp." Video: "Light finds [Subject] as a realization lands, the face becoming the brightest fact in the room." Name what caused the change (sun, door, lamp).

Use in Video Generator

Light finds [Subject] as a realization lands, the face becoming the brightest fact in the room.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a static cameo or a decorative volumetric shaft. The tell is no change, or brightness with no cause.

Fix it by starting darker and letting a motivated source find the face at the thought.

Questions

What is epiphany in film?

A lighting change that makes a person suddenly the brightest readable fact as a realization lands. The light is timed to understanding.

Epiphany vs cameo lighting

Cameo is a static isolated pool on a dark ground. Epiphany is a change: light finds the face because a thought arrives, often from a motivated source.

When should I use epiphany lighting?

Use it when a decision or insight should be visible in exposure. Skip it as decoration on a scene with no inner turn.

How do I prompt epiphany for AI image or video?

Describe a sudden intelligible brightness on the face as a realization lands. In video, start dimmer and let light find the subject. Name the cause.

entries.title: Spotlight
entries.text:
Spotlight

A spotlight in spotlight cinematography is a focused, hard-edged pool from a theatrical or similar instrument, with darkness around the circle. The person is treated as an act inside that pool.

Create this Spotlight

Narrative function

The stage is a circle of light. A drummer, a speaker, a dancer: the instrument has a beam you can see the edge of, and stepping out of it is stepping out of the scene.

Theatre and concert coverage use it because the world really is that lamp. It is the wrong tool for a motivated apartment, or for a soft cameo with no circle.

If the pool has no edge, you have a general key in a dark room. If the figure is isolated but the source is a large silk, that is cameo, not a spot.

How it works

Use a focused fixture (ellipsoidal, follow spot, PAR with a tight lens) with shutters or an iris so the pool has a hard edge. Place it high and frontal or high and slightly front-side, the theatrical default.

Hardness is hard; falloff at the circle is sudden. Color is often white or a theatrical gel.

The surround is unlit. Prompt: Spotlight on [Subject], a hard pool, theater darkness around, the person as an act.

When to use it

Use it when the stage is a circle of light, a solo, a speech, a club act. Do not use it as the key in a kitchen that has no such instrument.

Compared with similar shots

Cameo lighting is isolation; a spotlight is one hard instrument that can create that isolation with a visible circle. Hard light is the quality.

Top light may come from above without a circular shuttered pool. Cross lighting is two concert keys, not necessarily irised spots.

Epiphany is a story-timed change, which a spotlight snap can serve.

Cameo LightingErase the world. Keep the person.

Hard LightGrit, noon sun, or interrogation.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

Whiplash puts players in hard stage pools. Birdman's theatre scenes treat follow spots and stage lamps as the world of the act.

The edge of the circle is the set line.

Prompt it

Demand a hard pool and a dark surround. " Mention a visible circle or shuttered edge.

Forbid a large soft wrap.

Use in Image Generator

Spotlight on [Subject], a hard pool, theater darkness around, the person as an act.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a soft cameo or a general hard key. The tell is no circle, or wrap that lights the floor evenly.

Fix it by irising a focused fixture and letting the edge of the pool be visible.

Questions

What is a spotlight in film?

A focused, hard-edged pool from a theatrical or similar instrument, with darkness around. The subject stands in a circle of light.

Spotlight vs cameo lighting

A spotlight is the instrument and its hard pool. Cameo is the result of isolating a modeled figure on black, which can also be done with a softer key and no visible circle.

When should I use a spotlight?

Use it for stage, concert, and any beat where stepping out of the circle leaves the scene. Skip it in ordinary rooms with no such lamp.

How do I prompt a spotlight for AI image or video?

Specify a hard pool, theater darkness around, a visible circular or shuttered edge. The person is an act. No soft wrap on the floor.

entries.title: Glam
entries.text:
Glam

Glam lighting, in glam lighting terms, is a large beauty key with catchlights in the eyes and a little diffusion on skin, built to sell the face. It is a package of size, frontal or near-frontal placement, and skin treatment, not a single nose-shadow pattern.

Create this Glam

Narrative function

Fashion, stardom, a singer at a mirror: pores calm down, eyes live, the face is a product the camera can love. The key is large, often slightly high, and fill is generous enough that neither cheek dies.

It is the wrong tool for grit, illness, or a liar in a dark bar. Glam is not butterfly by default (butterfly is the Paramount nose shadow; glam can be loop or almost frontal).

It is not high-key unless the whole set is also bright. It is not generic soft light; a large side key can be soft and still un-glamorous.

How it works

Use a large source near camera, slightly above the lens, with optional bounce below so sockets do not hole. Hardness is soft.

Color is beauty-neutral or slightly warm (tungsten or daylight, not sick green). Add a weak hair edge if the set is dark.

Diffusion on the lens or source keeps speculars kind. Catchlights should sit in the irises as lamps, not grids projected on the face.

Prompt: Soft beauty key on [Subject], large source, catchlights inside the eyes, a little diffusion on skin. No projected squares or grids on the face.

When to use it

Use it to sell the face, a star close-up, a beauty still, a romantic hero the story wants us to want. Do not use it on a corpse, a boxing cut, or a documentary interview that should look found.

Compared with similar shots

Butterfly lighting is a specific high on-axis nose shadow often used inside glam. Soft light is only hardness.

High-key lighting is frame contrast. Eye light is the catchlight subset.

Three-point lighting can be glamorous if the key is large and frontal enough, but three-point includes a back that glam may skip. Naturalistic ambient hides this package on purpose.

Butterfly LightingBeauty lighting with structure.

Soft LightBeauty, memory, or kindness.

Three-Point LightingTeachable portrait. Start here, then break it.

In film

A Star Is Born (both the concert close-ups and the makeover grammar) uses large beauty keys when stardom is the product. Fashion films and work in the neighborhood of Carol or Phantom Thread sell faces with size, catchlights, and controlled skin, then withdraw the package when the story turns ugly.

Prompt it

Sell the face with physics, not a mood word. Use: "Soft beauty key on [Subject], large source, catchlights inside the eyes, a little diffusion on skin.

" Keep the key near camera. Forbid hard splits and overhead skulls.

Use in Image Generator

Soft beauty key on [Subject], large source, catchlights inside the eyes, a little diffusion on skin. No projected squares or grids on the face.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is butterfly with a small hard source, or a grid of catchlights printed on the skin. The tell is a razor nose shadow, hollow sockets, or square projections on the cheeks.

Fix it by enlarging the key, moving it near the lens, and keeping catchlights inside the irises only.

Questions

What is glam in film?

A large beauty key with catchlights and slight diffusion, designed to sell the face. It is a package of source size and placement, not a mood word.

Glam vs butterfly lighting

Butterfly is a high, on-axis key that makes a small shadow under the nose. Glam often uses that pattern but can be a large near-frontal key without a strict butterfly. Glam also includes catchlights and skin diffusion.

When should I use glam lighting?

Use it when the face is the product: fashion, stardom, romance the story wants to sell. Skip it for grit, horror, and found documentary.

How do I prompt glam for AI image or video?

Specify a large soft beauty key, catchlights inside the eyes, a little diffusion on skin, no projected grids on the face. Keep the key near camera.
